title: Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court to give evidence in his own defence
summary: Brand was due to testify for the first time as his trial moved to the defence case; he denies all seven counts of rape, sexual assault and indecent assault.

title: Brooklyn pastor sentenced to 14 years for years-long sexual abuse of a girl from his congregation
institution: Messengers for Christ World Healing Center
summary: Paul Lewis, pastor of a Brooklyn church, received 14 years in prison plus 10 years of post-release supervision after a jury convicted him in September of a course of sexual conduct against a child who attended his congregation.

title: Former Poudre School District high school counselor sentenced to 16 years in child sexual exploitation case
summary: Cassandra Poncelow, a longtime counselor in the Fort Collins-area district who was arrested in 2025 over alleged abuse of a student, pleaded guilty to two counts of sexual exploitation of a child. A Larimer County judge sentenced her to 16 years in prison followed by 10 years of intensive sex-offender probation.

title: Proposed class action seeks $10M from Detroit, saying police ignored warnings about ex-officer now charged with rapes
summary: A woman suing anonymously alleges the City of Detroit kept former officer Benjamin Wagner on patrol despite warnings and left thousands of rape kits untested; Wagner, arrested in March, faces kidnapping and criminal sexual conduct charges involving at least six women. The claims are unproven and the city had not commented.

title: Former Nova Academy charter school staffer charged with sexually abusing a teenage student in Coachella
institution: Nova Academy Early College High School
summary: Riverside County prosecutors charged a former staff member of the Coachella charter high school with multiple sex offenses involving a teenage student, following a sheriff's investigation that began with an October report. The school says she no longer works there; the charges are allegations.

title: House Judiciary Democrats release Epstein staff report, renew call for special counsel on DOJ handling
summary: Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee released a staff report compiling allegations involving President Trump and others tied to Epstein, including a newly reported 1993 rape allegation, and Rep. Jamie Raskin asked the Justice Department to appoint an independent special counsel. The White House denies the allegations.

title: Brand's former personal assistant describes his treatment of women as prosecution case nears its end
summary: In a statement read to the jury on the trial's tenth day, a woman who worked as Brand's assistant in 2006-07 said she saw him treat women poorly and quit from burnout, while saying she never saw him do anything illegal. The judge said the defence case would open on Tuesday; Brand denies all seven charges.

title: Ghana education ministry warns district directors they will answer for failing to report teacher abuse claims
summary: Speaking for the education minister after abuse allegations at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Deputy Minister Clement Apaak told education directors that every allegation against a teacher must be reported and the accused removed from contact with pupils pending investigation, and that directors who shield staff will be held accountable.

title: Vermont diocese's bid to exit bankruptcy heads to December hearing after creditors rejected $29.4M offer
summary: The Burlington diocese has asked to end its two-year Chapter 11 case, citing about $2 million in legal fees, after the claimants' committee rejected a $29.4 million offer for 119 abuse claimants. A judge is set to weigh dismissal on Dec. 8; claimants are also pursuing roughly $500 million in parish trust assets.

title: Ex-West Virginia delegate and fired Fayette County teacher facing child exploitation charges seeks release
summary: Elliott Pritt, a former state lawmaker and Fayette County social studies teacher who was fired after his arrest, has asked a federal court to release him to a VA residential mental health program while he awaits trial on child sexual exploitation, coercion and witness tampering charges. Prosecutors oppose the request.

title: SafeSport suspends Downriver Detroit youth soccer coach over alleged relationship with a minor player
summary: The U.S. Center for SafeSport lists a coach tied to the Wayne County club Chaos Soccer as suspended over an alleged intimate relationship involving a minor, and the state youth soccer association has imposed its own suspension. The coach, who has not been charged, disputes the grounds and is appealing; local police have been investigating since 2025.

title: Family sues LaRue County school staff, saying bus workers failed to stop repeated assaults on a young student
summary: A lawsuit in LaRue Circuit Court names the Kentucky district's superintendent and four other employees, alleging staff on a special-needs bus route failed to intervene as an older student sexually and physically assaulted a young child. The district had not responded to the allegations.

title: Judge dismisses negligence claims in Las Vegas suit alleging LDS bishop told abuse victim not to call police
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: Judge Jennifer Dorsey ruled Nevada law recognizes no general church duty to protect members, but gave the plaintiff 10 days to refile on the theory the church took on a duty when a bishop promised to handle her 1999 report of childhood abuse by a congregation teacher.

title: Family sues Catholic parish and Oklahoma City archbishop, saying youth program failed to report assault on their child
summary: A civil petition against St. Thomas More University Parish and Archbishop Paul Coakley alleges a child was sexually assaulted by another minor during a parish youth event and that the youth director did not report it to police. The family claims the parish failed to screen, train and supervise staff and volunteers and seeks at least $250,000.

title: Former inmate sues New Mexico corrections chief over sexual contact by guard at Grants women's prison
summary: A woman held at Western New Mexico Correctional Facility has filed a civil rights suit against a former guard and the state corrections secretary, saying the state failed to keep her safe in custody. The guard pleaded guilty last year to criminal sexual contact involving four women at the prison and received probation.

title: Dutch Reformed congregation sidelines minister's daughter after criminal abuse report; members fault months of silence
summary: Elders of the Reformed Congregation in Elspeet say they put the minister's daughter, a former youth choir conductor, on inactive status after a criminal report of sexual abuse was filed against her. Church members have criticized leaders for keeping quiet for months, and the council has said the minister made wrong judgments as her father.

title: Cornell student named in Jane Doe's fraternity suit asks court to dismiss claims against him as time-barred
summary: One of seven former Chi Phi members sued by a former Cornell undergraduate moved to dismiss, arguing the one-year limitations period had run and that the claims against him are narrow; all defendants deny wrongdoing. The state attorney general is investigating as special prosecutor and Cornell is conducting an internal review.

title: New York archdiocese confirms $800 million deal with about 1,300 abuse claimants; signing set for November
summary: After survivors' attorneys announced the agreement, Archbishop Ronald Hicks confirmed it to clergy; the deal, the second-largest by a U.S. archdiocese, becomes final only once the parties sign it, expected the week of Nov. 6.

title: Chicago archdiocese review board finds no reasonable cause in decades-old allegation, returns retired priest to ministry
summary: Cardinal Blase Cupich accepted his Independent Review Board's recommendation to close a case alleging a former South Side pastor abused a minor more than 30 years ago; the priest denied the claim, and the archdiocese says it was told a civil suit would be filed.

title: New York archdiocese nears deal of more than $800 million to resolve about 1,300 abuse claims
summary: Plaintiffs' lawyers say all claimants have accepted a settlement offering each at least $250,000 or a larger reviewed payout, plus an insurer-funded pool for holdouts and a published list of credibly accused clergy; the archdiocese says terms are still being finalized.

title: Former Newington College teacher faces nine sex charges involving a former student
summary: Deandra Kontou, who taught at the Sydney boys' school and later at a public college, is on bail on charges relating to a student in her care in 2019 and has been suspended without pay; the charges are unproven.

title: Belize evangelical body says complaints about charged pastor were ignored by church leaders years ago
summary: After pastor Kevin Tzib was charged with sexual assault and remanded, the association said victims had reportedly raised complaints with church leadership about five years ago without action and urged churches to act swiftly on such reports.

title: University of Arizona police investigating sexual assault report at Sigma Phi Epsilon house
summary: University police are investigating a student's report that she was sexually assaulted at the Sigma Phi Epsilon chapter house in August; no charges have been referred. Campus crime logs show about 20 rape or sexual assault reports since January, amid a broader crackdown on fraternity misconduct at the university.

title: Kansas Senate race ad revives scrutiny of megachurch's handling of 2005 youth retreat complaint
institution: United Methodist Church of the Resurrection
summary: Sen. Roger Marshall's campaign accuses Democratic nominee Adam Hamilton, the church's founding pastor, of failing to act on 2005 reports that a volunteer touched two teens at a retreat; the church's internal review was inconclusive and the volunteer was later convicted in a separate case. Hamilton says the claims are false and that the church should have called police at once and has since changed its policies.

title: Portugal closes all abuse complaints against living Catholic priests without a single indictment
summary: According to Expresso, 15 investigations stemming from the independent commission and 28 complaints sent to its successor body, Grupo Vita, were archived, mostly because the alleged offences were time-barred or evidence was judged insufficient.

title: Thirteen more women sue New Jersey OB-GYN practice, alleging former doctor abused patients during exams
institution: Delaware Valley OB-GYN and Infertility Group
summary: The Mercer County suit, which follows a 31-plaintiff case filed in July, accuses the Lawrence Township practice and affiliated companies of negligent oversight of a former physician whose license was temporarily suspended in 2024; he has not been criminally charged.

title: Baltimore archdiocese and survivors report progress in bankruptcy talks as judge urges year-end deal
summary: At a Chapter 11 hearing, the parties said the plan's structure is largely agreed and the dollar figure is the main sticking point; parishes and schools have joined the talks and three days of mediation are scheduled.

title: Lawton pastor charged with raping two boys over 13 years; associate accused of helping
summary: Pastor James Lamont Newton faces rape, sodomy and child lewdness counts, with police alleging he used his church role and gifts to control a victim; a second man is charged as an accessory, and investigators say earlier reports in 1998 and 1999 stalled.

title: Judge lets Jane Doe stay anonymous in suit against seven ex-members of Cornell's Chi Phi fraternity
summary: A New York judge cited the case's profile and the risk of threats in letting the plaintiff proceed under a pseudonym and signaled the defendants could seek the same. The seven men deny the alleged 2024 assault at the fraternity house; the ruling does not address the merits.

title: Duke says football staffer named in Rolesville High groping lawsuit is no longer working with team
summary: Duke called it a confidential personnel matter after reports on a civil suit accusing the former Rolesville High head coach of touching a ninth-grader in class; the Wake County school board is also a defendant. The claims are unproven and no criminal charge is reported.

title: Tufts sues to overturn arbitration award reinstating professor fired for sexual misconduct
summary: An arbitrator reduced the 2025 firing of a faculty member found to have violated Tufts' sexual misconduct policy to a written reprimand. Tufts asked a federal court to vacate the award, arguing reinstatement conflicts with its policy and public policy against workplace and campus misconduct.

title: Former eXp agent settles remaining sexual assault claims against two ex-recruiters
summary: The agent's confidential settlement with the two former recruiters follows earlier settlements with the brokerage and with CEO Glenn Sanford, who was accused of ignoring warnings and admitted no liability. A separate 2024 suit by four other agents is still pending.

title: Former Syracuse High students sue Davis School District over handling of shared nude and fake images
summary: Two former students filed a federal Title IX suit alleging administrators mishandled their 2023 reports that male classmates circulated intimate and doctored images of girls online and failed to discipline anyone. The district strongly disputes the allegations.

title: Lawsuit accuses Wake County schools of failing to supervise Rolesville High coach accused of groping student
institution: Wake County Public School System (Rolesville High School)
summary: A civil suit alleges a former Rolesville High teacher and football coach, now on Duke's football staff, groped a ninth-grader in 2025 and that the district failed to supervise him despite known concerns. The coach denies the allegations and has not been charged.

title: Teen files $10 million claim saying Marine Corps failed to supervise Sunnyvale recruiter who assaulted her
summary: A claim under the Federal Tort Claims Act alleges the Marines ignored Defense Department rules against closed-door meetings with prospective recruits and failed to supervise a recruiter who sexually assaulted a 17-year-old at the Sunnyvale recruiting office in 2024. The recruiter later took a plea deal requiring sex offender registration.

title: Grooming gangs inquiry announces first national accountability hearings for agencies and institutions
institution: UK National Inquiry into Grooming Gangs
summary: The statutory inquiry chaired by Baroness Longfield said organisations will have to explain what they did to protect children from exploitation, with opening hearings on survivors' experiences set for London in December and January and more planned for spring 2027. It also published its list of core participants.

title: Perry County, Kentucky Baptist pastor indicted on federal charges over sexual images of minors
summary: A federal grand jury in London, Ky., charged pastor Jared Salmons with producing obscene depictions of minors and receiving and possessing child sexual abuse material; the Kentucky Baptist Convention said it was aware of the case. The charges are unproven.

title: Peninsula School District settles suits over ignored warnings about convicted teacher for $23.2 million
summary: Families alleged administrators disregarded colleagues' concerns dating to at least 2019 about former Evergreen Elementary teacher Jordan Henderson, who was convicted of child molestation in January; the district's insurers are paying the settlement.

title: Federal indictment adds child sexual abuse material counts against former Lexington Baptist worship pastor
summary: Worship singer Richard Channing Shealy, an interim worship pastor at Lexington Baptist and River District churches, now faces nine federal counts on top of 33 state charges filed since his March arrest; he has not been convicted.

title: Soweto primary school teacher charged with raping pupil; Gauteng education chief promises suspension and vetting
summary: After protests, the teacher handed himself over to police; MEC Lebogang Maile said he will be suspended and pledged background checks for future appointments, while advocates questioned why the school did not act sooner.

title: Massachusetts lawmakers show little urgency on amendment ending child sex abuse lawsuit deadlines
summary: A House amendment to a health care bill would scrap the civil filing deadline for child sexual abuse claims, lift the charitable immunity cap and open a two-year lookback window, but it now sits in closed-door conference talks. The push follows the attorney general's report on abuse in three Catholic dioceses.

title: Former Calvary Chapel Montrose senior pastor arrested on child sex abuse charges
summary: Benjamin Garate, formerly senior pastor of the Colorado church, faces sex-related and child abuse charges and was held on a $60,000 bond. The church said he no longer works there, was removed from all leadership roles, and that it is cooperating with investigators.

title: More former Radford University students say Title IX process failed them after reported assaults
summary: Two more women told WDBJ7 they were sexually assaulted while students and described long, difficult Title IX and conduct proceedings with light sanctions. Radford cites privacy laws and says a presidential task force is reviewing its policies.

title: Schoenstatt movement asks for accounts about founder Kentenich as abuse allegations remain under study
summary: The German Catholic movement invited people who knew Fr. Joseph Kentenich to share memories and documents, including any experiences of abuse, as research into 2020 allegations of coercive conduct continues. His beatification cause has been suspended since 2022.

title: Oklahoma jury orders Pocola schools and ex-superintendent to pay $7.2 million over handling of abuse report
summary: A LeFlore County jury found Pocola Public Schools and former superintendent Jason Brittain each liable for $3.6 million after a student's 2021 abuse disclosures were routed to a state hotline rather than police. The jury found the former superintendent acted in bad faith; the district did not comment.

title: Disabled former resident sues Oregon for $9 million over alleged abuse by caretaker at state crisis unit
summary: The suit alleges a male Oregon Department of Human Services caretaker at the Macleay House stabilization and crisis unit isolated and repeatedly assaulted a disabled resident from 2023 to 2025, and that staffing rules requiring two workers including a woman were not followed. The agency declined to comment.

title: UConn fires Stamford history professor after third sexual harassment investigation
summary: The University of Connecticut terminated a Stamford campus history professor after its civil rights office found he created a hostile environment by pursuing a student through text messages, following two earlier complaints. He disputes the findings and can appeal through arbitration.

title: Former seminarian says he warned Derry diocese priests about Fr Edward Gallagher in the 1990s
summary: A former Maynooth seminarian says he raised grooming concerns about Fr Edward Gallagher with two senior Derry diocese priests decades before the priest pleaded guilty this month to more than 100 child sex offences. The diocese says it has no record of those complaints, and the bishop is asking the Vatican to dismiss Gallagher from the priesthood.

title: Jury convicts former Park City police officer of sexually abusing a woman while on duty
summary: A Lake County jury found former part-time Park City officer Patrick Cacho guilty on 20 counts including aggravated criminal sexual abuse and official misconduct for abusing a woman while on duty. Sentencing is set for December, and he faces lifetime sex offender registration.

title: Raskin accuses Justice Department of obstructing state and foreign probes of Epstein's associates
summary: In a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche, Rep. Jamie Raskin alleged the department is withholding evidence from New Mexico investigators and blocking UK requests in Epstein-related inquiries, and demanded records of foreign legal-assistance requests. The allegations come from committee Democrats.

title: Friends and a former colleague back account of woman alleging rape at Brand's home as trial enters day seven
summary: On the seventh day of Russell Brand's trial at Southwark Crown Court, friends and an ex-colleague of the complainant testified she told them soon afterward that he had raped her at his Hampstead home in 2009. Brand denies all seven counts.

title: Former Gilmour Academy hockey player sues school and coaches over alleged sexual hazing on Lake Placid trip
summary: A federal suit by a former player of the Ohio Catholic school's prep hockey team alleges teammates sexually assaulted him during a 2022 tournament trip and that coaches knew of a hazing ritual involving sexual misconduct. The school denies fostering a hazing culture and says the matter was investigated years ago; the claims are unproven.

title: FIFA extends Congolese coach's ban to 2048 and fines federation and club for letting him keep coaching
summary: FIFA's ethics committee added five years to the ban on Jonathan Bukabakwa, previously convicted in a child sexual abuse case, after reports he was still training young players in Kinshasa. The Congolese football federation and Racing Club Baki were each fined $50,000 for failing to enforce the original suspension.
location: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kinshasa

title: Former Wilmington Catholic school teacher goes on trial over alleged 1990s abuse of a student
summary: Christopher Crisona faces multiple felony counts tied to alleged abuse of a pupil at the now-closed parish school; the defense disputes the accuser's memories. A former priest at the school, John Taggart, faces separate charges with a trial set for January.

title: Bonduel associate principal charged with repeated sexual assault of a student
summary: Kaitlyn Hintz, associate principal of Bonduel Middle and High School in Wisconsin, made a first court appearance on charges including repeated sexual assault of a child and was held on $500,000 cash bond. The district placed her on leave after receiving a report on Oct. 15 and contacting police.

title: Cornell trustees hire Sally Yates to lead independent review of sexual assault response
summary: A special committee of Cornell's board retained former Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to examine the university's handling of a 2024 fraternity sexual assault report and its broader prevention, discipline and Greek-life oversight. The board says it will publish her findings.

title: Judge refuses to cut bond for ex-Riverview officer charged with assaulting detainee inside police station
summary: Former Riverview, Missouri, officer Torre' Dyson, charged with sexual conduct in the course of public duty, will stay jailed after a judge denied a bond reduction. Prosecutors allege he took a handcuffed woman to the station without notifying dispatch and assaulted her there; his license was already on probation.

title: Lawsuits say Florida church and Christian academy hired youth pastor despite warnings about him
summary: Two civil suits accuse the Christian and Missionary Alliance, Edgewater Alliance Church and Warner Christian Academy of giving a youth pastor access to children in 2004 despite an alleged warning from a relative about his conduct with boys. The man was investigated by police but never charged; the institutions had not commented in the report.

title: Ghana parliamentary committee demands probe of Obuasi school officials who allegedly ignored complaints
summary: Parliament's human rights committee urged police and the attorney-general to speed up the case against the arrested headmaster and to investigate staff who may have received earlier complaints without acting. It also asked education and gender ministries to support students and protect them from retaliation; the allegations remain unproven.

title: Former KIPP University Prep assistant teacher indicted on charges involving a student
summary: A Bexar County grand jury indicted a former assistant teacher at the San Antonio charter high school on indecency with a child and improper educator-student relationship charges over alleged conduct during school hours in 2025. The report did not include a response from the school.

title: Air Force officer's suit accusing Charlotte Marriott of lax security after hotel-room assault heads to trial
summary: A pseudonymous Air Force major alleges the Charlotte Marriott City Center let a known trespasser roam guest floors and failed to secure his room before a 2022 sexual assault; the intruder later pleaded guilty. The $160 million federal case is set for trial in November while the hotel defendants' summary judgment motion is pending.

title: Lawsuit accuses late Providence bishop Louis Gelineau of abusing an altar boy in the 1980s
summary: An anonymous plaintiff alleges he was abused at a Barrington parish by a credibly accused priest and by the former bishop, who died in 2024, and that the diocese ignored warning signs. It is one of dozens of suits filed since a June Rhode Island law reopened older claims; the diocese says it will respond in court.

title: Records show Oregon's Central School District received months of warnings before teacher's sex-crime charges
summary: District records show parents and students raised concerns about former teacher and coach Ian Imamura for about a year before the district opened an investigation in May 2026. Imamura has pleaded not guilty to felony sex charges involving a student; the district says every complaint was investigated.

title: Defence cross-examines youngest complainant over alleged 2009 rape at Brand's home
summary: Brand's barrister argued the woman's admiration for him clouded her judgement and that his conduct was not rape; she maintained she did not consent. Brand denies all charges.

title: New Mexico attorney general sues Epstein estate executors, alleging they enabled his abuse
summary: Attorney General Raul Torrez filed a federal civil suit against co-executors Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn, seeking to keep them from profiting and to direct estate assets to survivors. Both have denied involvement in Epstein's crimes.

title: Fortescue fires senior executive after external probe into harassment and bullying claims
summary: The iron ore miner said an unnamed executive breached its policies after a MinterEllison investigation into sexual harassment and bullying allegations. The company already faces a separate employee class action over alleged assaults at Pilbara mine sites.

title: Lawsuit says Cabrillo Unified ignored warning signs as former teacher and coach abused student for years
source: Business Wire (Cerri, Boskovich & Allard press release)
summary: A former student's suit in San Mateo County alleges district staff saw boundary violations by a teacher and coach, who recently pleaded no contest to a felony lewd-act charge, but did not report or stop abuse that allegedly began in middle school. The claims have not been tested in court.

title: Lawsuit says Bangor Wendy's operator ignored harassment reports and cut accuser's hours
summary: A former employee alleges in a Maine Human Rights Act suit that the company running a Bangor Wendy's kept scheduling her with a coworker she reported for repeated unwanted touching, then cut her hours and pushed her out. The company has not commented.

title: Bolivian survivors call Jesuits' expulsion of a laicized Catalan priest an empty gesture
summary: After a church process found the Catalan former priest guilty and the order expelled him, a Bolivian survivors' network said the move is symbolic because he still lives in a Jesuit residence under restrictions. A Spanish court earlier ruled he could not be prosecuted because the time limit had expired.

title: Cornell disputes Jane Doe's account that president questioned her delay in reporting alleged gang rape
summary: In a letter to the faculty senate, the former student suing Cornell over an alleged 2024 fraternity gang rape said she felt disbelieved by President Michael Kotlikoff; the university says the remark was misreported. The letter surfaced as faculty weigh a no-confidence resolution and the state attorney general takes over as special prosecutor.

title: Dallas ISD to pay $1 million to settle DOJ claims it failed to report a teacher's alleged misconduct
summary: Federal prosecutors said the district closed misconduct complaints against a former special education teacher instead of reporting them to state certification officials; most of the money funds reforms. The district disputes the allegations.

title: Federal judge dismisses childhood sexual abuse suit against OpenAI CEO Sam Altman with prejudice
summary: A Missouri federal judge threw out a family member's suit alleging Altman abused her as a child, finding she refused a court-ordered medical evaluation and intentionally delayed the case. Altman has called the claims completely untrue; OpenAI was not a party.

title: Jury hears from sixth complainant as Brand trial turns to alleged assault at his home
summary: Prosecutors began presenting the allegations of a sixth woman, playing parts of her police interview in which she says an encounter at Brand's home turned non-consensual a week after consensual contact. Brand denies all seven charges.

title: Lawsuit accuses Alpha Delta Phi and University of Chicago of ignoring years of assault reports at chapter
summary: An anonymous student's Cook County suit alleges she was assaulted at a February fraternity party and that the fraternity and university knew of sexual assault reports at the chapter dating to 2009 but required no safeguards. The fraternity says it suspended the member; police are still investigating.

title: Seventeen Democratic attorneys general urge Congress to pass second Epstein files bill
summary: In a letter to congressional leaders, state attorneys general backed Rep. Thomas Massie's bill requiring the Justice Department to share unredacted Epstein records with state and local prosecutors. The department says withheld files are duplicates, unrelated or privileged.

title: Massachusetts AG meets clergy abuse survivors, renews push to end statute of limitations
institution: Dioceses of Worcester, Springfield and Fall River
summary: Weeks after her report on three dioceses, Attorney General Andrea Campbell met privately with survivors and described her office's push to lift time limits, remove the charitable immunity cap and open a lookback window. Some survivors said investigators never contacted them.

title: Amazon employee sues, saying company failed to protect her after she reported rape by a senior manager
summary: An unnamed Amazon employee alleges in a new suit that the company kept her working alongside a senior manager she reported for raping her on a 2023 company-funded trip and ran an inadequate investigation. Amazon's internal review found insufficient evidence of a policy violation; police closed their inquiry without charges.

title: Mercer Island School District claim over alleged teacher grooming settles for $1.5 million
summary: A former Mercer Island High School student's $13.4 million claim, alleging administrators failed to stop a longtime English teacher's grooming and abuse about 15 years ago, was resolved before suit for $1.5 million. The district's insurance pool pays the full amount and there is no admission of liability.

title: Woman sues Kansas priest, Diocese of Salina and Kansas City archdiocese alleging misconduct cover-up
summary: An adult woman alleges Rev. Ryan McCandless, already facing unrelated child sex charges, used a spiritual-counseling relationship to coerce her into sexual contact in 2024, and that the Diocese of Salina, the Kansas City archdiocese and a Manhattan parish concealed her report. The archdiocese says he never served there; Salina declined comment.

title: Ghana's Obuasi Senior High Technical headmaster arrested as police probe students' abuse allegations
summary: Several female students have accused the school's headmaster of sexual misconduct; the education minister ordered him interdicted and police say he was arrested, with one rape docket sent to the Attorney-General for advice. Activists question whether earlier complaints were ignored by school and education authorities.

title: Judge upholds Maryland Child Victims Act against WWE challenge, letting ring boys suit proceed
summary: U.S. District Judge James Bredar rejected a due process challenge by WWE, TKO, Vince McMahon and Linda McMahon to applying Maryland's 2023 Child Victims Act to alleged abuse of ring crew boys in the 1980s and 1990s. The suit by seven anonymous plaintiffs now moves toward discovery; the defendants deny the allegations.

title: Federal judge dismisses suit accusing Southern Baptist Convention of giving sex offender access to children
summary: Judge Richard Gergel dismissed, for lack of jurisdiction, a lawsuit by parents of a Pawleys Island Christian Academy student alleging the SBC and its Executive Committee let a convicted sex offender keep access to children. The ruling did not decide the underlying allegations.

title: Fourth complainant tells Brand trial of alleged assault at Choice FM studios
summary: A former radio station worker testified that Brand sexually assaulted her at Choice FM's London studios in the mid-2000s and said the workplace culture deterred her from reporting it. Brand denies the charge.

title: Channel 4 worker tells trial she reported Brand to the broadcaster in 2009
summary: A woman who worked on a Channel 4 project in 2009 testified that she was pressured into massaging Brand, who then laid his head in her lap, and that she reported it to her line manager the next day. Brand denies the sexual assault charge; Channel 4 had earlier apologised for failing to investigate a 2009 complaint.

title: Jury sees police interview of woman alleging rape at Brand's Hampstead home in 2009
summary: Jurors watched the recorded police interview of a woman who met Brand after a Hammersmith Apollo show in 2009 and says consensual sex at his home became non-consensual when he did not stop; police photos of the house were shown. Brand denies the rape charge.

title: Loyola University Chicago students protest as Title IX mishandling lawsuit heads toward 2027 trial
summary: Students rallied on campus over a lawsuit by ten former students alleging the university mishandled and underreported sexual assault complaints dating back to 2011. The university has failed to get the case dismissed, and a trial is set for September 2027; Loyola declined to comment on pending litigation.

title: KQED investigation details staff sexual abuse and retaliation at Chowchilla women's prison
institution: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation
summary: A two-year KQED and CalMatters investigation found internal affairs knew of a convicted officer's misconduct at Central California Women's Facility for months before acting, and that women who reported staff abuse faced retaliation. Hundreds of related civil suits are consolidated in Sacramento.

title: Mangalore diocese parish priest arrested under India's child protection law over abuse of boys
summary: Police in Karnataka arrested a parish priest of the Diocese of Mangalore in a POCSO case alleging abuse of several boys. Local reports say the diocese placed him on leave in August and initially handled the matter internally; the bishop declined comment.

title: Former executive pastor at The Chapel and youth soccer coach sentenced to eight years for child sex abuse
summary: John Camardo III, a former executive pastor at the Western New York megachurch who also coached girls' travel soccer in Amherst, received eight years in prison after pleading guilty to rape and sexual conduct against a child, Erie County prosecutors said.

title: Il Fornaio agrees to $3 million settlement of EEOC sexual harassment suit
summary: The EEOC alleged the restaurant chain ignored harassment of female workers, many of them teenagers, at locations in California and Nevada. The company denied wrongdoing and agreed to an outside monitor and HR reforms.

title: Albemarle County presses school board after principal and two staffers charged with failing to report abuse
summary: County supervisors asked the school board for more transparency and a whistleblower system after a teacher was charged with abusing elementary students and three administrators were charged with not reporting. The charged teacher denies the allegations.

title: Taunton State Hospital nurse sues Massachusetts agencies over alleged workplace assault and retaliation
summary: A nurse alleges the state kept a coworker on the job despite two earlier complaints before he allegedly assaulted her in 2025, then tried to reassign her while colleagues retaliated. The coworker faces criminal charges and has pleaded not guilty; the department says it acted promptly and later fired him.

title: Lawsuit says Horry County Schools ignored warning signs before Aynor High teacher's arrest
summary: A family's suit alleges a former Aynor High School teacher groomed a student and sent explicit material, and that district staff knew or should have known and failed to intervene. The teacher was arrested in 2025 on related criminal charges and resigned; the district has not commented on the suit.

title: Vatican upholds Lafayette bishop's excommunication of deacon whose son was abused by a priest
summary: The Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith rejected a former deacon's appeal of his excommunication, which followed his departure from the Church over the abuse of his son by Father Michael Guidry, who confessed and is serving a prison sentence. Critics note the bishop let Guidry remain a priest.

title: Reformed Church of Zurich apologizes after review finds it mishandled abuse by a former vicar
institution: Reformed Church of the Canton of Zurich
summary: An external report found at least ten women suffered sexual, physical and psychological abuse by a former vicar between 1992 and 2006, and that the church closed its 2007 inquiry without acknowledging the confirmed abuse. The church council apologized and pledged to handle future cases differently.

title: eXp Realty settles one agent's sexual assault suit as trial against two ex-recruiters begins
summary: eXp Realty and parent AGNT reached a confidential settlement with an agent who alleged she was sexually assaulted by company-affiliated recruiters, without admitting wrongdoing, as her federal trial against two former recruiters opened in Los Angeles. A separate suit by four other women naming eXp is still pending.

title: Third complainant alleges Brand orally raped her in a Soho bar toilet in 2004
summary: A former MTV worker told the jury Brand groped her within a minute of meeting at a London bar in 2004 and then pulled her into a toilet where she says he forced a sex act on her; her 2023 police interview was played. Brand denies the charges.

title: Defence tells third complainant the alleged toilet assault was physically impossible
summary: Under cross-examination, Ian Winter KC suggested the woman went willingly with Brand, that others would have seen any assault, and that she only called it rape after the 2023 coverage; she disputed his account. Brand denies the charges.

title: Survivors ask New Hampshire Supreme Court to roll back YDC fund changes
summary: Survivors' attorneys argued the state breached a binding agreement by giving the attorney general veto power over awards. The state contends no binding contract existed.

title: Former student sues Evergreen Public Schools, alleging district failed to stop band teacher's abuse
institution: Evergreen Public Schools (Mountain View High School)
summary: A former Mountain View High School student filed suit in Clark County Superior Court alleging the district failed to protect her from years of grooming and sexual abuse by a band teacher in the early 2000s. The claims are allegations and have not been tested in court.

title: Georgetown updates clerical abuse page after reporting on a Jesuit's alleged misconduct with students
summary: After the student paper reported that a late Jesuit priest allegedly harassed at least four students and returned to campus after a 1998 complaint, Georgetown revised its Title IX page to acknowledge a 2010 finding of unwanted touching and disclosed new protocols for sharing Jesuit misconduct reports.

title: Second complainant says Brand tried to drag her into toilets at MTV in 2001
summary: A former MTV Europe worker testified that Brand grabbed her arm and tried to pull her into the men's toilets before she freed herself; the defence called it a brief, minor incident. Brand denies the indecent assault charge.

title: Former flatmate tells trial sex was a preoccupation for Brand in the late 1990s
summary: A former flatmate and member of Brand's cabaret troupe gave evidence about the 1999 Bournemouth trip, describing Brand as egotistical and recalling he did not return with the group one night. Brand denies all charges.

title: First complainant tells jury Brand raped her after 1999 Labour conference event
summary: The jury watched the police interview of the first complainant, who alleges Brand raped her in her hotel room in Bournemouth in 1999, before she gave evidence from behind screens. Brand denies the charge.

title: Defence challenges first complainant's memory as jury is shown 1999 hotel photos
summary: Defence barrister Ian Winter KC suggested the first complainant had reimagined a consensual encounter and questioned discrepancies in her account, using photos she took in the hotel room; she rejected his suggestions. Brand denies the charge.

title: Englewood school district sued over alleged abuse by after-school program aide
summary: A new lawsuit against the Englewood school board, the city and an elementary school alleges officials knew or should have known about the conduct of a former after-school program aide who was arrested in 2023 on multiple sexual assault charges. The suit claims negligence and failure to supervise; the district had not commented.

title: Prosecution opens case, describing Brand as a calculated and manipulative predator
summary: Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC told jurors six women who did not know each other would describe alleged assaults at a hotel, workplaces including broadcasters, a bar and Brand's home. Brand denies all charges and has told police encounters were consensual or that he does not recall them.

title: Lyft asks federal judge to narrow consolidated passenger sexual assault lawsuits
summary: At a hearing in San Francisco, Lyft argued that negligence and product liability claims in roughly 136 consolidated federal suits by riders alleging assault by drivers should be dismissed. The judge voiced skepticism of some of Lyft's arguments but did not rule from the bench.

title: Cornell president acknowledges he never followed up on 2024 fraternity gang-rape report
summary: Cornell's president said he did not check the outcome of a student's 2024 report of a fraternity gang rape, as a lawsuit alleges the university mishandled her complaints and the faculty senate weighs a no-confidence resolution. New York's governor named the state attorney general special prosecutor and ordered an independent review of Cornell's handling of the case.

title: Jury sworn in for Russell Brand rape and sexual assault trial
summary: A jury was sworn in after the judge excluded potential jurors who had seen coverage of the allegations and told them not to research the case. Brand firmly denies all seven charges.

title: Brand trial opens at Southwark Crown Court with jury selection
summary: Jury selection began in Brand's trial on three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009. Brand, who is on bail, denies all charges.

title: Federal judge rejects Oakland Diocese bankruptcy plan covering about 330 abuse claims
summary: A federal bankruptcy judge declined to confirm the Oakland Diocese's Chapter 11 plan meant to resolve roughly 330 clergy abuse claims, citing insufficient evidentiary support. The judge indicated a revised plan could still be approved.

title: Former Menlo-Atherton student sues Sequoia Union High School District over alleged teacher abuse
institution: Sequoia Union High School District (Menlo-Atherton High School)
summary: A former student filed suit in San Mateo County alleging a former teacher sexually abused her between 2006 and 2010 and that the district failed to supervise, investigate, warn students or report the teacher to police. The district did not respond to requests for comment.

title: Uber settles third bellwether passenger assault case in Texas just before opening statements
summary: Uber reached a confidential settlement with a Texas rider shortly after jury selection in the third bellwether trial of the federal passenger sexual assault litigation. Thousands of similar cases remain pending in the multidistrict litigation in California.

title: Judge rules police searches of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes unlawful
summary: A London judge found Thames Valley Police made significant errors obtaining warrants used to search the former prince's properties in its Epstein-related inquiry.

title: Education Department opens probes into NYC schools and Jeffco over staff sexual misconduct handling
institution: New York City Department of Education
summary: The U.S. Education Department's Office for Civil Rights launched investigations into how the New York City school system, Colorado's Jeffco Public Schools and unnamed districts in six other states handle sexual misconduct claims against employees, targeting so-called pass-the-trash practices. New York City schools said they take abuse allegations seriously and are reviewing the complaint.
location: United States, New York and Colorado

title: Second former student joins Child Victims Act suit against Montgomery County school board
summary: An amended complaint adds a second former elementary student to a lawsuit alleging the school board negligently kept a teacher in roles with access to children despite complaints dating to 1993 and a 1995 child protective services finding. The suit relies on Maryland's Child Victims Act; the allegations are unproven.

title: Massachusetts AG report finds hundreds of clergy abused nearly 1,000 children in three dioceses
institution: Dioceses of Worcester, Springfield and Fall River
summary: The Massachusetts attorney general released the state's first investigation into clergy abuse in three Catholic dioceses, finding that more than 270 clergy abused close to 1,000 children going back to the 1950s. The report notes Worcester remains the only diocese in the state without a public list of credibly accused priests.

title: Scouting abuse trust has paid about $1.3 billion to 50,000 survivors as fees draw scrutiny
summary: The Scouting Settlement Trust had distributed nearly $1.3 billion to just over 50,000 survivors, while about $40 million had gone to trustee and legal fees. Approved claimants were expected to receive only a small share of their claims' assessed value.

title: Jury awards $164 million against College Park hotel operator in child sex trafficking case
summary: A federal jury in Atlanta found the operator of a College Park Super 8 liable under federal trafficking law, concluding it knew or should have known of trafficking at the property and profited from it. The verdict totaled $164 million.

title: Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison in New York retrial case
summary: A Manhattan judge sentenced Weinstein to 15 years for the 2006 sexual assault of Miriam Haley; he maintains his innocence and still awaits resentencing in Los Angeles.

title: New lawsuit seeks to block Epstein advisers from inheriting millions
summary: Survivors sued to stop estate co-executors Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn from receiving bequests, alleging they enabled Epstein's abuse; the pair deny it.

title: Family sues Savannah nursing home alleging cover-up of resident sexual assault
summary: A lawsuit in Chatham County alleges a Savannah nursing facility failed to protect a nonverbal resident from sexual assault by another resident with a known history of misconduct and delayed informing her family. The facility had not responded to the allegations.

title: House holds Leon Black in contempt of Congress
summary: The House approved a resolution holding Black in contempt for defying its Epstein subpoena, referring the matter to federal prosecutors.

title: Woman pleads guilty to defrauding Epstein victims' compensation fund
summary: A Florida woman who received $750,000 from the estate-funded Epstein Victims' Compensation Program pleaded guilty to falsifying records in her claim.

title: Former federal prison worker sentenced for sexual contact with inmates at FCI Thomson
summary: Danny L. Spyker, a former corrections officer and cook supervisor convicted by a federal jury of sexual contact with inmates, was sentenced to three years and five months in prison. Prosecutors said he abused his position of authority over people in custody.

title: Lawsuit alleges former Burnet County jail officer sexually abused a detainee
summary: A former detainee filed a federal lawsuit against Burnet County and former detention officer Michael Jason Wilson alleging he sexually abused her in custody in 2024. The article notes Wilson was previously convicted on felony counts involving abuse of a different detainee; the new claims are allegations.

title: Survivors' lawyers say Al Fayed claims could reach £150m as talks stall
summary: KP Law, representing more than 275 alleged survivors, said settlement talks with Harrods and the Fayed estate had stalled pending litigation involving the estate.

title: Appeals court tosses Dan Schneider's 'Quiet on Set' defamation suit
summary: A California appellate panel unanimously ruled for the docuseries' makers under the anti-SLAPP law, finding the show did not defamatorily imply Schneider abused children.

title: Lawsuit alleges Genesis Health Clubs trainer groomed and abused a teenage member
summary: A former member alleges in a Jackson County, Missouri, lawsuit that a personal trainer at a Kansas City Genesis gym sexually abused her when she was a minor in 2021. The suit accuses the chain of negligent hiring, supervision and training.

title: Sandusky forgoes recantation testimony as lawyers prepare federal bid
summary: Appearing remotely from prison, Sandusky told a judge he agreed with his lawyers not to present the recanting accuser's testimony as they prepare to seek a new trial in federal court.

title: Combs' projected prison release date moves again
summary: Bureau of Prisons records listed a new projected release date of Feb. 5, 2028, for Combs, who is serving his sentence at Fort Dix.

title: Leon Black skips Epstein deposition and sues House committee
summary: The former Apollo CEO refused to appear for a sworn deposition about his $158 million in payments to Epstein and sued to block the subpoenas.

title: Sandusky seeks to cancel recantation hearing and take case to federal court
summary: Sandusky's lawyers asked to cancel the scheduled hearing, and Sandusky said in a prison recording that he wanted to pursue his claims in federal court.

title: Former Cal softball player sues UC Regents, alleging coach pursued coercive sexual relationship
summary: A former pitcher sued the University of California Regents and a former head softball coach, alleging a coercive sexual relationship and that the university was negligent in hiring, training and supervising staff who allegedly knew and did not intervene. The coach's tenure ended in 2025 shortly after the university received a report about the relationship.

title: Diocese of Ogdensburg seeks to exit bankruptcy with $83 million abuse fund
summary: The northern New York diocese proposed an $83 million survivor fund, including insurer contributions, to conclude its bankruptcy case.

title: Florida court enters judgment against prison health contractor over gynecologist abuse claims
summary: A federal court entered a $100,000 judgment in a civil case brought by five women prisoners alleging sexual abuse by a contracted gynecologist at Lowell Correctional Institution. The suit also alleged the state prison health contractor tolerated the conduct despite complaints; the doctor denies the allegations.

title: Court filings say one Sandusky accuser signed affidavit recanting testimony
summary: Sandusky's lawyers said one of the trial witnesses signed an affidavit recanting, and a judge set an evidentiary hearing; the attorney general's office called the recantation highly suspect.

title: Appeals court orders new trial after $10 million verdict against Carnival in shipboard assault suit
summary: The 11th Circuit vacated parts of a $10.3 million Miami jury award to a passenger who alleged a crew member sexually assaulted her aboard a Carnival ship in 2018. The court ruled the jury should have been allowed to hear evidence from an FBI report and ordered a new trial.

title: Ireland's schools abuse commission invites survivors to share experiences in national survey
institution: Religious-run and other Irish schools (Commission of Investigation)
summary: The state Commission of Investigation into historical sexual abuse in Irish schools is launching a survey of people abused in schools between 1927 and 2013 to identify patterns and guide its inquiry. A 2024 scoping inquiry had identified more than 2,300 allegations at 308 religious-run schools, and a redress scheme is expected to follow.

title: Judge rejects Maxwell's habeas bid to overturn conviction
summary: Judge Paul Engelmayer rejected Maxwell's claims that new evidence warranted vacating her conviction, calling them meritless.

title: Former child actor sues Disney alleging company failed to protect her from on-set abuse
summary: A negligence lawsuit filed in Los Angeles County Superior Court alleges a Disney employee sexually abused a minor actor during a 2001 Disney Channel production and that the company failed to protect her or investigate. Disney could not be reached for comment.

title: Pentagon survey finds unwanted sexual contact down, more troops reporting
summary: The fiscal 2025 report found prevalence fell among active-duty women and men, while about a third of those affected reported, up from a quarter in 2023.

title: Judge rules ex-Abercrombie & Fitch CEO Mike Jeffries competent to stand trial on sex trafficking charges
summary: A federal judge in Brooklyn found former Abercrombie & Fitch CEO Mike Jeffries mentally fit for trial on sex trafficking and interstate prostitution charges, reversing a 2025 finding. Jeffries is accused of exploiting male models while leading the company; jury selection was set for late October 2026.

title: Pentagon report shows estimated military sexual assaults fell for third straight year
summary: The Pentagon's fiscal 2025 report estimated about 20,500 active-duty members experienced sexual assault, down from earlier surveys, while formal reports rose to nearly 8,000. Advocacy groups questioned whether the decline reflects actual conditions.

title: Johnny Hunt appeals dismissal of defamation suit to Sixth Circuit
summary: Hunt filed a notice of appeal after the district court dismissed all his claims against the SBC, Guidepost and Barber.

title: Phillips Academy alumni report abuse by school's former medical director
summary: Two alumni reported they were sexually abused as students by the boarding school's former medical director, who served from 1992 to 2011 and was later convicted on federal child pornography charges. School leaders invited others to come forward and said they are working with an outside nonprofit on a survivor-centered policy review.

title: Pornhub owner Aylo agrees to pay $120 million to settle child sexual abuse material class actions
summary: Aylo agreed to a $120 million settlement, pending court approval, of two U.S. class actions alleging that videos of minors were uploaded to Pornhub without consent. The company denies the allegations but agreed to identity verification, moderation measures and outside audits.

title: Texas and Roblox clash over discovery in state child-safety lawsuit
summary: Texas's attorney general, who accuses Roblox of marketing itself as safe while failing to protect children from predators, says the company has been slow to turn over documents. Roblox calls the requests overbroad; a tentative trial date is set for 2028.

title: Judge dismisses Johnny Hunt's final defamation claim
summary: The court rejected Hunt's last remaining claim against Bart Barber, ruling Hunt was a public figure who failed to show actual malice.

title: Raleigh rider files $50 million lawsuit against Lyft over alleged assault by driver
summary: A North Carolina rider sued Lyft in Durham County alleging a driver sexually assaulted her during a ride in March 2026; the driver has been criminally charged and indicted. Lyft said it does not comment on pending litigation.

title: Louisiana family sues Roblox and Discord alleging platforms enabled sexual exploitation of a teen
summary: A lawsuit filed in Northern California alleges an adult groomed a Louisiana minor on Roblox and moved the contact to Discord, where exploitation followed. The suit claims both companies misled parents about child safety on their platforms.

title: Ex-Kentucky swim coach settles abuse suit; claims against University of Kentucky head to 2027 trial
summary: A former University of Kentucky head swim coach, previously banned for life by the U.S. Center for SafeSport, settled claims brought by two former swimmers alleging sexual assault and a hostile environment. The lawsuit's claims against the university and its former athletic director remain active, with trial set for May 2027; both deny wrongdoing.

title: Interlochen-commissioned report details decades of abuse allegations against nearly 50 adults
summary: An outside investigation commissioned by the Michigan arts boarding school documented about 70 allegations of sexual abuse by nearly 50 affiliated adults from the 1950s to the 2010s, including Jeffrey Epstein, and cited gaps in oversight and a permissive environment. The school apologized, referred names to law enforcement and created a counseling fund, though some alumni say the response falls short.

title: New Mexico judge orders Meta to pay $567 million and tighten protections for minors
summary: A Santa Fe judge found Meta created a public nuisance and ordered $567 million for a teen mental health fund plus a five-year decree including tighter limits on adult contact with minors and enhanced review of child sexual abuse reports. Meta said it will appeal.

title: Tribunal upholds complaint against priest who failed to report Smyth disclosure
summary: A disciplinary tribunal found Canon Andrew Cornes neglected his duties by not reporting a 1982 disclosure and imposed a conditional discharge.

title: Arizona Supreme Court rules church leaders not bound to report abuse confessions
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: The court unanimously reinstated dismissal of the Bisbee lawsuit, holding the clergy exemption shielded bishops from reporting confessions.

title: New Mexico sues Justice Department claiming it blocked state Epstein probe
summary: New Mexico sued the Justice Department and acting Attorney General Blanche, alleging they withheld records needed for its investigation.

title: Jury orders Harrisville Central School District to pay $3.5M over 1980s teacher abuse
summary: A state Supreme Court jury ordered the Lewis County district to pay $3.5 million to a former student who alleged a teacher abused him in the early 1980s and that the district took no action after his parents reported it to the principal. The teacher died in 2018, and it is unclear whether the district will appeal.

title: B.C. court approves $30M class-action settlement over abuse at two Vancouver Catholic schools
institution: Vancouver College and St. Thomas More Collegiate
summary: The B.C. Supreme Court approved a $30-million settlement of a class action by more than 200 former students alleging historical sexual, physical and psychological abuse at the two schools, including by Christian Brothers transferred from Newfoundland's Mount Cashel orphanage. The deal sets up a confidential claims process instead of a trial.

title: Court approves $3M attorney fee deal in FCI Dublin sexual abuse class action
summary: A federal court approved a $3 million settlement covering attorneys' fees in the class action over staff sexual abuse of women at the now-closed FCI Dublin. Related litigation has produced roughly $130 million in payouts to more than 130 former prisoners.

title: Federal appeals court says insurers may have to cover church's West Virginia abuse settlement
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: The 10th Circuit reversed a ruling for the church's insurers over settlements tied to abuse by Michael Jensen and sent the case back.

title: Investigation finds misconduct reports at Michigan arts school Epstein funded
summary: An outside investigation for the Interlochen school, where Epstein was a major donor, found two former attendees reported sexual conduct by him and uncovered allegations against nearly 50 others over decades.

title: Nine more former detainees allege sexual abuse at Clark County juvenile detention center
summary: Nine adults filed notices of intent to sue Clark County, alleging county employees sexually abused them as youths held at the juvenile center between 1990 and 2014. The claims bring the total number of claimants against the county to 17.

title: Snohomish and Pierce counties ask court to make Washington state liable for juvenile abuse claims
summary: Prosecutors for two Washington counties asked a judge to designate the state as the proper defendant in sexual abuse claims tied to county juvenile detention centers, arguing state-appointed judges controlled staffing. The counties estimate potential exposure in the hundreds of millions of dollars.

title: Weill Cornell Medicine reaches compliance deal ending federal probe tied to convicted urologist
summary: Weill Cornell agreed to fund a $30 million patient-safety institute and strengthen abuse prevention to resolve a federal criminal investigation over its handling of former urologist Darius Paduch, who was sentenced to life for abusing patients. The institution previously agreed to pay more than $1 billion to settle civil claims.

title: Former WWE employee's suit against Vince McMahon and WWE moves to private arbitration
summary: A former WWE employee who accused ex-chairman Vince McMahon of sex trafficking and abuse agreed with McMahon and WWE to resolve her federal lawsuit in private arbitration, with the court case to be dismissed. McMahon has denied the allegations.

title: Eight more former detainees sue San Diego County over alleged abuse in juvenile facilities
institution: San Diego County Probation / juvenile detention facilities
summary: Eight anonymous plaintiffs filed a federal lawsuit alleging guards sexually abused them while they were held in San Diego County juvenile facilities. The case adds to similar claims from hundreds of former residents.

title: Acting AG Blanche meets Epstein survivors ahead of confirmation vote
summary: Todd Blanche, nominated as attorney general, met with Epstein accusers after a Republican senator made it a condition of his support.

title: Southwest Airlines sued over alleged in-flight sexual assault by intoxicated passenger
summary: A passenger alleges Southwest allowed an intoxicated man to board a Seattle-to-Sacramento flight and served him more alcohol before he assaulted her; the man pleaded guilty in federal court to simple assault. The negligence suit claims the airline failed to train staff and follow its own policies.

title: Education Secretary issues teacher sexual misconduct guidance, opens probes into 20 districts
institution: U.S. K-12 districts (including Tulare City and Wilsona, CA; LAUSD)
summary: Following reporting that California failed to revoke credentials of dozens of educators found to have committed sexual misconduct, the U.S. Education Department issued guidance threatening funding for schools that fail to protect students and opened investigations into 20 districts' handling of staff misconduct. It also opened an inquiry into LAUSD's reassignment policy for accused employees.

title: UK to change law to allow deportation of Rochdale gang leader
summary: The government said it would change the law to enable deportation of Shabir Ahmed after Pakistan refused to accept him.

title: Former detainees file new suit alleging sexual abuse at Snohomish County's Denney juvenile center
institution: Snohomish County, Denney Juvenile Justice Center
summary: Nine former detainees filed a negligence lawsuit alleging staff sexually abused them at the Denney juvenile facilities between the 1980s and 2012. The county said it is reviewing the complaint.

title: Maryland claims immunity from some Child Victims Act suits; top court agrees to hear it
summary: The state Supreme Court agreed to hear Maryland's argument that it is immune from some claims, a challenge that could end hundreds of suits.

title: Lawsuit accuses Gillespie County of failing to supervise deputy accused of on-duty sexual assault
summary: A woman filed a civil suit alleging a former sheriff's deputy sexually assaulted and harassed her while on duty in 2025, and that the county failed to properly screen and supervise him. The former deputy faces separate pending criminal charges unrelated to sexual assault; the civil claims are allegations.

title: Executive Council approves $20 million more for YDC settlements
summary: The council approved $20 million to continue settling claims from people abused at the former youth center, and the administrator said consultant rates would be cut.

title: Burnham presses for deportation of Rochdale ringleader on release
summary: Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham said nothing was off the table as concern grew over the release from prison of convicted Rochdale ringleader Shabir Ahmed, who could not be deported.

title: Cook County jury awards $50 million against Peoria climbing camp over assault of young camper
institution: First Ascent Climbing and Fitness Camp
summary: A Cook County jury found the operators of a Peoria children's climbing camp negligent in supervision after a camper was sexually assaulted by another camper in 2022. The award totaled $50 million, including punitive damages.

title: Archdiocese of San Francisco reaches $395 million abuse settlement
summary: A mediated $395 million deal in the archdiocese's bankruptcy would resolve more than 500 claims and require publication of a list of credibly accused priests.

title: San Francisco Archdiocese reaches $395 million deal with abuse survivors in bankruptcy
source: The New York Times (via GV Wire)
institution: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of San Francisco
summary: The Archdiocese of San Francisco agreed to pay $395 million to resolve about 530 childhood clergy abuse claims as part of its Chapter 11 case. The deal requires claimant and bankruptcy court approval and includes non-monetary child-protection commitments.

title: Judge rejects D.A.'s bid to pause L.A. County abuse settlement payments
summary: A Los Angeles Superior Court judge denied the district attorney's request to halt payments on the settlement covering more than 11,000 claims. Survivors' lawyers had argued that delays would harm ill or financially struggling claimants.

title: California appeals court upholds Weinstein's Los Angeles conviction but orders resentencing
summary: A California appellate court affirmed Weinstein's 2022 rape conviction but vacated his 16-year sentence and sent the case back for resentencing.

title: Prosecutors drop unresolved rape charge against Weinstein, avoiding fourth trial
summary: Manhattan prosecutors dropped the remaining rape charge after Jessica Mann said she would not proceed with a fourth trial; the judge dismissed the count while Weinstein's other convictions stand.

title: Maryland Supreme Court rules public schools immune from pre-1971 abuse claims
summary: The court held that victims cannot sue public school systems for abuse that occurred before mid-1971, when governmental immunity applied.

title: Michigan AG report reviews abuse allegations against 38 clergy in Diocese of Saginaw
summary: Michigan's attorney general released a report of more than 250 pages on sexual misconduct allegations involving 37 priests and a deacon in the Diocese of Saginaw, the sixth in a series of statewide reports. No criminal charges resulted, as most incidents predated 2002.

title: New Hampshire YDC abuse fund gets $20 million as new administrator aims to clear 1,700 claims
institution: State of New Hampshire, Youth Development Center settlement fund
summary: Lawmakers allocated $20 million, well below the requested $55 million, to pay claims from people abused at the state's former youth detention center. The fund's new administrator plans to resolve about 1,700 pending claims within three years.

title: UK national grooming gangs inquiry names first areas for investigation
institution: UK National Inquiry into Grooming Gangs
summary: The national statutory inquiry into child sexual exploitation by grooming gangs named London, Bradford, Keighley and Oldham as its first local investigation areas. It will examine how police, councils, health and social services responded.

title: Rhode Island opens two-year window for revived child sexual abuse lawsuits
summary: Governor Dan McKee signed legislation changing the statute of limitations for child sexual abuse claims and creating a window through June 2028 for previously time-barred suits against institutions. The law followed a state attorney general report on the Diocese of Providence.

title: Judge dismisses Dawn Richard's lawsuit against Combs as time-barred
summary: A federal judge dismissed former Bad Boy artist Dawn Richard's 2024 abuse suit against Combs because the claims were filed after New York's limitations periods expired.

title: D.A. seeks court order halting $4 billion settlement payouts, estimates most claims may be fraudulent
summary: Hochman asked a Superior Court judge to freeze juvenile hall claim payouts through Dec. 31, 2026, estimating up to 81% of claims could be fraudulent. Plaintiffs' attorneys disputed the estimate.

title: Bill Gates testifies to House panel about Epstein ties
summary: Gates told the House Oversight Committee that Epstein tried to use knowledge of an extramarital affair to pressure him.

title: SBC annual meeting turns to other issues as abuse reforms stall
summary: Ahead of the 2026 meeting, reporting found SBC leaders seeking to move past the abuse crisis with key reforms unfinished.

title: Records show South Jersey district paid $3.1M to settle teacher abuse suits
summary: Previously undisclosed settlements released after a public records case show the district and its insurers paid at least $3.125 million over lawsuits alleging a former teacher, who later pleaded guilty, abused boys over more than a decade. Deposition testimony indicated officials had raised boundary concerns years before his arrest, and two suits remain pending.

title: Ohio State agrees to roughly $100 million settlement with remaining Strauss plaintiffs
summary: Ohio State trustees approved a preliminary agreement of about $100 million with all but one of 280 survivors still in litigation.

title: Ohio State trustees approve about $100M settlement with former athletes over team doctor abuse
summary: Ohio State's board approved a preliminary settlement of roughly $100 million covering nearly all of the 280 remaining claimants who said a late university doctor abused them, adding to more than $61 million paid earlier. An independent report previously found university staff knew of complaints as early as 1979 but failed to act.

title: New Mexico Epstein 'Truth Commission' issues first subpoenas
summary: A bipartisan state commission investigating Epstein's activities in New Mexico issued 14 subpoenas at its first meeting.

title: Judge denies Cosby a new trial, upholding $59 million verdict
summary: A Los Angeles County judge rejected Cosby's bid for a new trial, leaving the roughly $59 million civil judgment in place.

title: Complaint filed over alleged sexual abuse of children in Western Australia youth detention
summary: Lawyers lodged a complaint with the Australian Human Rights Commission on behalf of about 100 people alleging sexual abuse in WA's youth detention system, including by custodial staff. A class action may follow if conciliation fails.

title: Crime and Policing Act 2026 creates mandatory duty to report child sexual abuse
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The Crime and Policing Act, which received Royal Assent on 29 April 2026, introduced a statutory duty for people in child-facing roles in England to report child sexual abuse, one of IICSA's main recommendations.

title: UK police open inquiries into historic child abuse allegations from Epstein files
summary: Surrey Police said they were investigating two decades-old child sexual abuse allegations identified in the U.S. Justice Department's Epstein records.

title: Weinstein's third New York trial ends in mistrial after jury deadlock
summary: A Manhattan judge declared a mistrial after jurors said they were hopelessly deadlocked on the rape charge involving Jessica Mann.

title: Special magistrate appointed for Child Victims Act cases against Maryland
summary: The Maryland Supreme Court appointed a special magistrate to manage common issues in the thousands of suits against the state.

title: Epstein survivors testify at congressional Democrats' hearing in West Palm Beach
summary: Survivors spoke at a shadow hearing held by House Oversight Democrats in Palm Beach County, pressing for accountability from the Justice Department.

title: Harrods redress scheme has fully compensated more than 75 Al Fayed abuse survivors
summary: Harrods' compensation scheme for people abused by former owner Mohamed Al Fayed reports 259 survivors in the process, with more than 75 fully compensated and nearly 200 claims pending. Police and the IOPC continue separate inquiries into enablers and past police handling.

title: Dozens compensated under Harrods scheme as watchdog probes five officers
summary: More than 75 claimants had been fully compensated with about 200 claims still pending, while the police watchdog investigated five current and former Met officers over past handling of complaints.

title: Judge releases note Epstein's cellmate says he found after 2019 incident
summary: A federal judge made public a note that Epstein's former cellmate said he found after Epstein's first suspected suicide attempt in jail in July 2019.

title: Final FCI Dublin officer sentenced, closing largest federal prison sex abuse prosecution
summary: Former prison medic Jeffrey Wilson was sentenced to about 4.3 years for sexually abusing an incarcerated woman, the last sentencing among the 10 charged.

title: Calgary judge approves payouts in John Ware School abuse class action against CBE
institution: Calgary Board of Education (John Ware School)
summary: A judge approved tiered payouts totaling about $15.8 million from the Calgary Board of Education to more than 50 former students who alleged abuse at John Ware School between 1988 and 2004. The board apologized, and the settlement gives survivors a role in shaping policy and training.

title: State drops charges against former YDC worker after two hung juries
summary: Prosecutors dropped sexual assault charges against Victor Malavet after two trials ended in deadlocked juries, deciding against a third trial.

title: Justice Department inspector general audits handling of Epstein files
summary: The department's internal watchdog launched an audit of how it handled and released Epstein-related records.

title: Weinstein's third New York trial opens on remaining rape charge
summary: Opening statements were set in Manhattan in a third trial on the rape charge involving Jessica Mann, with Weinstein held at Rikers Island amid reports of declining health.

title: Uber found liable in second federal bellwether trial over driver misconduct
summary: A federal jury in a North Carolina case found Uber liable for a driver's battery of a rider and awarded $5,000, after the judge ruled Uber is a common carrier under state law. Uber noted jurors found battery rather than sexual assault.

title: Lawsuit against Massage Envy follows sexual abuse charge against Lexington therapist
summary: A client sued Massage Envy in Fayette Circuit Court alleging it failed to supervise staff and implement safeguards after a therapist at its Lexington location was charged with first-degree sexual abuse. The suit also alleges the franchise concealed known risks across its locations.

title: Bankruptcy judge sets claims deadline in El Paso Diocese abuse case
summary: A federal bankruptcy judge set a September deadline for survivors to file abuse claims against the Diocese of El Paso after its Chapter 11 filing. The claims will shape a payment plan that survivors must vote on.

title: Former IU basketball players appeal dismissal of suit over team doctor exams
summary: Five former Indiana University men's basketball players are appealing a federal judge's ruling that their lawsuit, alleging the university and a former head trainer failed to stop abusive exams by a late team doctor, was filed too late. The plaintiffs argue the limitations period should run from when they recognized the conduct as abuse.

title: Ohio State settles with 13 Strauss survivors for $1.8 million
summary: New agreements with 13 survivors brought Ohio State's total to 317 survivors and more than $61 million.

title: Heaps pleads guilty to 13 counts and is resentenced to 11 years
summary: After his conviction was overturned, Heaps pleaded guilty to 13 felony counts involving five patients and was again sentenced to 11 years.

title: Cosby seeks new trial, calls $40 million punitive award excessive
summary: Cosby's lawyers moved for a new trial in the 1972 assault case, arguing the punitive damages were excessive and that the judge wrongly excluded certain evidence.

title: Appeals judges question severity of Combs' four-year sentence
summary: At oral argument, members of a 2nd Circuit panel questioned whether Combs' sentence for prostitution-related convictions was excessive; prosecutors defended it.

title: Maryland faces potential $60 billion liability from child sex abuse claims against state
summary: More than 12,000 claims have been filed against Maryland government entities under the Child Victims Act, with some lawmakers estimating exposure could reach $60 billion. Questions remain over which damages cap applies and how the state would pay.
