title: 11th Circuit revives three sex trafficking lawsuits against metro Atlanta hotels
summary: A federal appeals court reinstated three previously dismissed lawsuits alleging Atlanta-area hotels facilitated trafficking of minors, sending them toward trial. The precedential ruling applies across Georgia, Florida and Alabama.

title: Trump fires Attorney General Pam Bondi
summary: Trump removed Bondi, whose tenure was dogged by the Epstein files controversy; Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche became acting attorney general.

title: Bank of America to pay $72.5 million to Epstein survivors
summary: A federal judge preliminarily approved Bank of America's $72.5 million settlement of claims that it enabled Epstein's sex trafficking finances.

title: Final terms of reference published for national grooming gangs inquiry
summary: The home secretary accepted Baroness Longfield's changes to the inquiry's remit, including attention to ethnicity and culture and coverage back to 1996, with statutory powers from 13 April 2026.

title: BBC ends contract with Radio 2 host Scott Mills amid reports of closed historical police probe
summary: The BBC said presenter Scott Mills is no longer contracted to it, following media reports linking him to a past police investigation into historical sexual offence allegations. Prosecutors found insufficient evidence to bring charges and the case was closed in 2019; Mills did not comment.

title: Judge moves Brand trial to October 2026 so all seven charges can be heard together
summary: Mr Justice Bennathan moved the trial from June to 12 October 2026, citing time pressures and juror availability, with all seven charges to be tried together over an estimated two months. Brand denies all the charges.

title: Albany diocese strikes $148 million deal with abuse survivors
summary: About three years into its bankruptcy, the Diocese of Albany reached a $148 million settlement with a committee of survivors, its parishes and affiliates.

title: Executive Council confirms new YDC settlement fund administrator
summary: The Executive Council unanimously confirmed Gov. Ayotte's choice to run the YDC settlement fund following the 2025 restructuring.

title: Woman sues Planet Fitness alleging assault by known problem patron at South Carolina gym
summary: A member alleges in a negligence suit that another patron sexually assaulted her in a West Ashley Planet Fitness and that staff later described him as a known problem. The company had not responded to requests for comment.

title: New lawsuit accuses Paramus Catholic and Archdiocese of Newark of ignoring coach's abuse
summary: A former student filed a civil suit alleging a former hockey coach abused him on campus and on school trips, and that the school, the Archdiocese of Newark and the Christian Brothers knew and failed to act. It is one of dozens of suits involving the late coach; the archdiocese declined to comment.

title: Santa Fe jury orders Meta to pay New Mexico $375 million in child exploitation case
summary: A jury found Meta willfully violated New Mexico's consumer protection law by misrepresenting platform safety, including the extent of child sexual exploitation, and awarded the state $375 million. Meta said it would appeal.

title: Jury finds Cosby sexually assaulted woman in 1972, awards nearly $60 million
summary: A Santa Monica civil jury found Cosby liable for drugging and assaulting a former restaurant worker in 1972, awarding $19.25 million in compensatory damages and $40 million in punitive damages.

title: Maryland faces about 12,000 juvenile justice abuse claims with no payout plan
summary: Roughly 12,000 people allege abuse in the state's juvenile justice system, with potential liability in the billions and disputes over which cap applies.

title: California AG finds systemic failures at El Monte Union High School District, imposes court-supervised reforms
institution: El Monte Union High School District
summary: An 18-month state investigation prompted by reporting on misconduct at Rosemead High found systemic shortfalls in how the district responded to sexual abuse and harassment complaints, including discarded disciplinary records. A settlement requires a compliance coordinator, centralized records and four years of court oversight.

title: Judge orders former Ohio State president Gordon Gee to sit for deposition
summary: A federal judge granted plaintiffs' motion to compel former president E. Gordon Gee to be deposed in the Strauss litigation.

title: Federal guard at Brooklyn's MDC indicted on sexual abuse charge
summary: Correctional officer James Johnson was charged in a federal indictment with sexually abusing a detainee in 2025 and lying to federal agents. He was released on bail and has not been convicted.

title: House committee subpoenas Attorney General Bondi over Epstein files
summary: The House Oversight Committee subpoenaed Bondi to testify about the Justice Department's handling and release of the Epstein files.

title: External report confirms Columbia failures; OB-GYN chair and ex-dean step down
summary: A 156-page external report described a culture of silence that let Hadden's abuse continue; OB-GYN chair Mary D'Alton stepped down and former dean Lee Goldman is retiring.

title: Former students file federal suit alleging Oconto Falls schools ignored staff abuse for years
summary: Three former students sued the Oconto Falls Board of Education in federal court, alleging at least nine staff members groomed or abused at least 14 students between 2005 and 2025 and that the district enabled it. The district says prior allegations were investigated and referred to police; the claims are unproven.

title: New Mexico authorities search Epstein's former Zorro Ranch
summary: State authorities searched the ranch Epstein once owned as part of a renewed criminal investigation.

title: Police question three women as suspects in Al Fayed enabling investigation
summary: The Met questioned three women under caution over alleged trafficking and facilitating offences linked to Al Fayed; no arrests were made and 154 people had come forward.

title: Former student files $13.4M claim against Mercer Island School District over alleged teacher abuse
summary: A former student's tort claim alleges administrators received reports about an English teacher's relationship with her in 2012 but conducted a cursory review and did not contact police until 2024. The district declined to comment, citing pending legal proceedings.

title: McDonald's franchisee to pay $80,000 to resolve EEOC harassment suit involving teen worker
summary: An Oklahoma McDonald's franchisee agreed to a consent decree paying $80,000 and adopting anti-harassment policies and training to settle an EEOC suit over harassment of a minor employee. The franchisee denies the allegations.

title: Rhode Island AG report details decades of clergy abuse in Diocese of Providence
summary: Attorney General Peter Neronha released a multi-year investigation into clergy abuse and the diocese's handling of it, summarizing 72 clergy deemed credibly accused. The report recommended reforms including extending certain limitations periods.

title: New York attorney general investigates Columbia's handling of Hadden
summary: The state attorney general's office opened an investigation into how Columbia handled warnings about Hadden.

title: L.A. County counsel investigates law firm over possibly fraudulent AB 218 abuse claims
summary: County counsel launched an investigation into DTLA Law Group and others over potentially fraudulent claims, with Supervisor Kathryn Barger voicing support. The firm has denied wrongdoing.

title: Bill Clinton questioned by House investigators about Epstein
summary: The former president sat for a deposition in the House Oversight inquiry, saying he did nothing wrong in his association with Epstein.

title: Syracuse diocese receives final court approval of $176 million settlement
summary: The bankruptcy court issued a final decree allowing the Diocese of Syracuse to emerge from Chapter 11 after its $176 million survivor settlement.

title: Harvard places Martin Nowak on leave amid renewed Epstein investigation
summary: Harvard put the mathematics professor on paid administrative leave as it reopened scrutiny of his Epstein ties after the federal files release.

title: Larry Summers to resign from Harvard after Epstein revelations
summary: Summers said he would resign his Harvard professorship following disclosures about his relationship with Epstein.

title: New Hanover County school board approves settlement tied to convicted former teacher
summary: The board unanimously approved a settlement, reported at $640,000, with three more former students of a science teacher who pleaded guilty in 2019 to dozens of child exploitation charges. Plaintiffs alleged a principal's failure to act allowed the abuse to continue; an earlier case settled for $5.75 million without admission of wrongdoing.

title: Brand pleads not guilty to additional rape and sexual assault charges
summary: At Southwark Crown Court, Brand denied the two charges added in December 2025, bringing the total to seven counts involving six women, all of which he denies.

title: Epstein estate agrees to pay up to $35 million to settle suit against his advisers
summary: The estate agreed to resolve a class action alleging Epstein's lawyer Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn aided his trafficking; they denied wrongdoing.

title: LAUSD approves up to $250M more in bonds to pay sexual abuse settlements
summary: The LAUSD board authorized up to $250 million in bonds for abuse settlements, its second such authorization in a year, bringing the total to about $750 million. The wave of claims follows a 2019 state law extending the deadline for childhood abuse claims against public entities.

title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office
summary: British police arrested the former prince following revelations in the Epstein files about his conduct as a trade envoy; he was not charged at the time.

title: Diocese of Camden agrees to $180 million clergy abuse settlement
summary: The bankrupt Diocese of Camden agreed to a $180 million settlement, including $87.5 million from an earlier 2022 deal, subject to court approval.

title: Jewell School District pays $2.35M over claims it ignored complaints about convicted shop teacher
summary: The rural Oregon district settled a federal lawsuit alleging administrators failed to act on multiple complaints about a shop teacher, later convicted of sex crimes, and let him resign quietly and work with younger children elsewhere. The settlement was reached in 2025 but only recently made public.

title: Families pursue legal action against Bright Horizons after nursery worker jailed for child abuse
summary: Former Bright Horizons nursery worker Vincent Chan was sentenced to 18 years after admitting dozens of offences including abuse at a now-closed north London nursery. About 50 families have joined legal action accusing the company of ignoring safeguarding concerns; the company says it is reviewing its practices.

title: Judge orders former trustee Les Wexner to testify in Strauss case
summary: A federal judge refused to quash a subpoena and ordered Les Wexner, a former Ohio State board chair, to be deposed about what he knew of Strauss.

title: Maxwell invokes Fifth Amendment before House committee, seeks clemency
summary: Maxwell declined to answer House Oversight questions, citing her Fifth Amendment rights, while her lawyer sought clemency from Trump.

title: Appeals court sets April hearing in Combs appeal
summary: The 2nd Circuit scheduled oral argument for April 2026 in Combs' expedited appeal.

title: Files show FBI concluded Epstein did not run trafficking ring for powerful men
summary: Released records showed FBI investigators found evidence Epstein abused young women and girls but not that he trafficked them to other prominent men.

title: Uber loses first federal passenger sexual assault trial with $8.5 million verdict
summary: A federal jury in Phoenix found Uber liable on an apparent-agency theory for a driver's alleged assault of a rider and awarded $8.5 million, while rejecting negligence and design-defect claims. Uber said it would appeal.

title: Ohio State settles with eight more Strauss survivors
summary: Eight new settlements totaling $800,000 brought Ohio State's total to 304 survivors and more than $60 million.

title: Appeals court overturns Heaps conviction and orders retrial
summary: A California appeals court overturned Heaps's 2022 conviction because the trial judge did not share a jury note questioning a juror's English proficiency; prosecutors vowed to retry him.

title: Irish abuse survivor describes apology from Pope Leo after private audience
summary: An Irish survivor said Leo listened and apologized during a private meeting at the Vatican.

title: DOJ pulls thousands of Epstein files that exposed victim information
summary: The department said it removed thousands of documents and media that may have inadvertently revealed survivors' identities and was fixing redactions.

title: D.A. asks L.A. County to hold off on early abuse settlement payouts during fraud probe
summary: The district attorney asked the county to delay early payments from the $4 billion settlement for at least six months while investigators examine suspected fake claims. The county agreed to fund a settlement trust but withhold payments pending further review.

title: Justice Department releases 3 million pages of Epstein files
summary: The largest release yet included millions of pages, images and videos and new details about the earlier federal investigation and Epstein's contacts.

title: City of Sanger pays $5.25 million over former officer's sexual assaults
summary: Sanger settled a claim for $5.25 million brought by a woman assaulted by former officer J. DeShawn Torrence, who was convicted in federal court and is serving multiple life sentences. More claims against the city may follow.

title: Rochdale grooming trial collapses over jurors' messaging group
summary: A Rochdale grooming trial collapsed after it emerged that jurors had been communicating in a WhatsApp group.

title: Brand appears by video link from US on two new charges and is bailed
summary: Brand appeared by video link at Westminster Magistrates' Court on the additional rape and sexual assault charges and was granted bail to appear at Southwark Crown Court.

title: Winnsboro ISD superintendents arrested on charges of failing to report child abuse
summary: The district's former and current superintendents and another employee were arrested on charges including failure to report child abuse with intent to conceal, with affidavits alleging officials covered up two cases involving staff and students. Their counsel indicated they will plead not guilty.

title: Judge returns LA County foster-care abuse cases to trial track amid settlement delays
institution: Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services
summary: A judge ordered dozens of foster-care abuse lawsuits against Los Angeles County to move toward trial while the county's large juvenile abuse settlement remains in distribution. The court warned that settlement delays do not pause filing deadlines.

title: Women held at LA County jail allege sexual abuse by deputies in federal suit
institution: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, Century Regional Detention Facility
summary: Thirty-eight plaintiffs in a federal case allege widespread sexual misconduct by deputies at the women's jail in Lynwood. The Sheriff's Department says it is investigating the claims.

title: Supreme Court declines to hear challenge to $2.46 billion Boy Scouts abuse settlement
summary: The Supreme Court denied review without comment, leaving the Third Circuit ruling and the plan's third-party releases in place. The decision frees about $1.65 billion in escrowed insurer funds, and Scouting America said payments to survivors could now accelerate.

title: Judge dismisses survivors' lawsuit over changes to YDC settlement fund
summary: A Merrimack County judge dismissed former residents' suit claiming Gov. Kelly Ayotte weakened the fund. Survivors said they would appeal.

title: Trump says he will not pardon Sean Combs
summary: President Trump said he was not planning to pardon Combs after reports that Combs had sought clemency.

title: Springfield to pay nearly $15M to settle suits alleging school ignored abuse reports
summary: The city of Springfield agreed to pay close to $15 million to settle two lawsuits alleging a former middle school teacher harassed and assaulted students whose reports to staff were repeatedly dismissed. The school department plans $1 million in staff training on recognizing and reporting grooming.

title: Contract officer pleads guilty to sexually abusing detainee at Louisiana ICE facility
institution: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, South Louisiana ICE Processing Center
summary: Former contract detention officer David Courvelle pleaded guilty in federal court to sexual misconduct with a person in federal custody at the Basile, Louisiana, facility. The charge carries up to 15 years in prison.

title: DOJ misses deadline, says completing Epstein release may take weeks
summary: The department said it had found more than a million additional potentially relevant documents and needed more time, drawing bipartisan criticism.

title: Brand charged with one further count of rape and one of sexual assault involving two more women
summary: The CPS authorised two additional charges, one of rape and one of sexual assault, relating to two further women and alleged offences in 2009. The Met said its investigation remained ongoing; Brand denies wrongdoing.

title: Justice Department begins releasing Epstein files under new law
summary: On the law's deadline, the department began posting Epstein investigative files, with heavy redactions and only part of the material released.

title: Federal judge lets WWE 'ring boys' abuse lawsuit proceed to discovery
summary: A federal judge in Maryland allowed a lawsuit to move into discovery that alleges WWE and Vince and Linda McMahon knew of and failed to stop sexual abuse of underage ring crew workers decades ago. Linda McMahon's lawyer called the suit baseless.

title: Women sue Match Group alleging Hinge and Tinder let convicted Denver doctor keep using apps
summary: Six women allege in Denver District Court that Match Group's apps kept recommending Stephen Matthews, later convicted of multiple sexual assaults, after receiving complaints about him. Match Group said it is committed to improving its safety tools.

title: Michigan AG report details abuse by 51 priests in Diocese of Grand Rapids
summary: Attorney General Dana Nessel released a report on the Diocese of Grand Rapids naming 51 priests, part of her statewide clergy abuse investigation.

title: Florida attorney general sues Roblox over alleged failure to protect children from predators
summary: Florida's attorney general sued Roblox alleging it facilitates sexual exploitation of minors and misrepresents its safety, in violation of state consumer protection law. Roblox said the suit misrepresents how its platform works.

title: New York archdiocese to raise $300 million to settle 1,300 abuse claims
summary: Cardinal Timothy Dolan said the archdiocese would enter mediation and raise more than $300 million through budget cuts, layoffs and property sales to resolve about 1,300 abuse claims.

title: Baroness Longfield named chair of national grooming gangs inquiry
summary: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood appointed former children's commissioner Anne Longfield to lead a three-year, £65m national inquiry and published draft terms of reference.

title: Federal judge approves New Orleans archdiocese bankruptcy settlement
summary: A federal judge confirmed the Archdiocese of New Orleans' plan to compensate hundreds of abuse survivors, ending a bankruptcy of more than five years.

title: YDC settlement fund payouts top $237 million with nearly 1,700 claims pending
summary: The fund had resolved 419 of 2,269 claims for more than $237 million, with 1,697 still pending and potential liability estimated near $2 billion.

title: More than 10,000 suits against Juvenile Services loom over Maryland's budget
summary: With a $1.4 billion deficit, lawmakers faced more than 10,000 abuse claims against the Department of Juvenile Services and no settlement plan.

title: Federal judge approves Archdiocese of New Orleans bankruptcy plan with abuse fund
institution: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of New Orleans
summary: A federal judge confirmed a plan ending the archdiocese's long bankruptcy, including a $230 million compensation fund for clergy abuse survivors. Additional money is expected from an insurer and parishes.

title: Judge allows release of abandoned Florida Epstein grand jury transcripts
summary: Citing the new transparency law, a federal judge permitted the Justice Department to release transcripts from the 2000s federal grand jury probe in Florida.

title: Scouting America urges Supreme Court to reject challenge to its bankruptcy deal
summary: The organization told the justices the petitioners represent a tiny fraction of claimants and that the $1.65 billion insurance-rights sale funding the trust closed years ago and cannot be undone. It argued bankruptcy law bars the relief sought.

title: Chicago Board of Education approves $17.5M settlement over former dean's abuse of student
institution: Chicago Public Schools (Greater Lawndale High School for Social Justice)
summary: The board approved a $17.5 million settlement with a former student abused by a dean of students who was convicted and sentenced to 22 years; the suit alleged staff saw warning signs and did not act. CPS denied wrongdoing but said it settled to avoid the toll of a trial.

title: New Hampshire Supreme Court hears arguments over $38 million YDC verdict
summary: The justices heard arguments on the state's liability and whether the $475,000 cap applies to the landmark award.

title: L.A. County D.A. opens criminal probe into alleged fraud in $4.8 billion abuse settlements
summary: District Attorney Nathan Hochman's office began investigating attorneys and others suspected of submitting false claims to share in the settlements. The probe followed reporting that some plaintiffs were steered to a law firm and paid to fabricate claims.

title: Prosecutors drop charges against last FCI Dublin guard after two hung juries
summary: Federal prosecutors moved to dismiss charges against Smith; nine other former employees, including the warden, were convicted or pleaded guilty.

title: Trump signs Epstein Files Transparency Act
summary: After near-unanimous votes in Congress, Trump signed a law requiring the Justice Department to release its Epstein files within 30 days.

title: Larry Summers steps back from Harvard teaching as university reviews Epstein ties
summary: Former Harvard president Larry Summers stopped teaching while Harvard investigated his correspondence with Epstein revealed in released emails.

title: Danny Masterson asks court to overturn rape convictions over attorney errors
summary: Danny Masterson filed a habeas petition arguing his trial lawyers were ineffective and asking that his convictions and sentence be vacated.

title: Bondi orders federal probe of Epstein's ties to Clinton and others at Trump's urging
summary: Attorney General Bondi assigned a federal prosecutor to investigate Epstein's ties to Bill Clinton and other figures Trump named, a move critics said could delay records releases.

title: House Democrats release Epstein emails referencing Trump
summary: Oversight Committee Democrats released emails from the Epstein estate referencing Donald Trump; the White House called the release a smear and Trump denied wrongdoing.

title: California judge denies Roblox bid to force child exploitation lawsuit into arbitration
summary: A San Mateo County judge rejected Roblox's motion to compel arbitration in a family's suit alleging its child was exploited after contact on Roblox and Discord, keeping the case in open court. Roblox said it would appeal.

title: Combs transferred to Fort Dix federal prison
summary: Combs was moved to the low-security FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey to serve his sentence.

title: Combs seeks expedited appeal of conviction and sentence
summary: Combs' lawyers asked the 2nd Circuit to fast-track his appeal, arguing his sentence improperly relied on acquitted conduct.

title: Andrew stripped of prince title and ordered out of Royal Lodge
summary: King Charles moved to remove his brother's remaining titles, including prince, after renewed scrutiny of his ties to Epstein; he became Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.

title: L.A. County supervisors approve $828 million child sex abuse settlement
summary: Supervisors approved the $828 million payout and said every claim in both settlements would be reviewed. Officials acknowledged the claims system created under AB 218 was vulnerable to fraud.

title: Child Victims Act cases resume in Baltimore court after five-month pause
summary: Cases in Baltimore City Circuit Court resumed after a temporary stay.

title: Second candidate to chair national grooming gangs inquiry withdraws
summary: Former police officer Jim Gamble withdrew from consideration to chair the national inquiry after Annie Hudson did the same, as several survivors quit the inquiry's liaison panel.

title: Former foster parents sue Clearfield County child welfare agency over undisclosed abuse history
institution: Clearfield County Children, Youth and Family Services
summary: A former foster couple filed a federal lawsuit alleging the county agency placed a teen in their home without disclosing his history of abusing other children, leading to harm in the household. The claims are allegations.

title: Pope Leo XIV meets survivors' advocacy group at Vatican
summary: Leo held his first meeting with leaders of Ending Clergy Abuse, who pressed for a global zero-tolerance law.

title: L.A. County reaches $828 million deal to settle about 400 more abuse claims
summary: Los Angeles County tentatively agreed to an additional $828 million settlement covering roughly 400 more claims of sexual abuse in county youth facilities and foster care. The deal comes on top of the earlier $4 billion accord.

title: More plaintiffs say they were recruited to file false claims in L.A. County abuse settlement
summary: Additional plaintiffs told the Times they were recruited and told to invent abuse claims filed as part of the $4 billion settlement. The law firm denies involvement, and genuine survivors voiced fears the allegations would overshadow real cases.

title: Guam-based abuse claimants ask Supreme Court to review Boy Scouts settlement
summary: A group of Guam-based claimants petitioned the Supreme Court, arguing the plan's releases for local councils, churches and schools conflict with the Purdue Pharma ruling. The petition kept roughly $1.5 billion in escrow, leaving survivors with about 1.5% recoveries so far.

title: Varsity Brands and former owner Bain Capital named in $200 million cheer abuse lawsuit
summary: A Gwinnett County, Georgia, lawsuit alleges Varsity Brands, Bain Capital, USA Cheer and others failed to safeguard young athletes from a cheer coach accused of sexual exploitation, including RICO claims. Varsity rejects the claim that it enabled such conduct.

title: L.A. County orders investigation of attorneys after report that plaintiffs were paid to sue
summary: Supervisors unanimously directed county counsel to examine possible wrongdoing by attorneys tied to the abuse lawsuits and set up a tip line. The move followed Times reporting that some plaintiffs were allegedly recruited and paid to file claims, which the law firm denies.

title: Supreme Court declines to hear Ghislaine Maxwell's appeal
summary: The Supreme Court turned away Maxwell's argument that Epstein's 2008 non-prosecution agreement barred her prosecution, leaving her conviction intact.

title: Sean Combs sentenced to 50 months in prison
summary: Judge Subramanian sentenced Combs to 50 months in prison and a $500,000 fine on the Mann Act convictions.

title: Sandusky files appeal alleging new evidence of prosecutorial misconduct
summary: Sandusky, still maintaining his innocence, filed a new petition claiming prosecutors coached witnesses and that a medical condition limited him physically. Prosecutors have contested his repeated appeals.

title: Robert Morris pleads guilty to child sex abuse charges
summary: Morris pleaded guilty and received a 10-year sentence with six months in jail, probation and sex offender registration.

title: Ringleader of Rochdale grooming gang jailed for 35 years
summary: The leader of the Rochdale gang convicted in June 2025 received a 35-year sentence, with co-defendants also jailed.

title: Jury deadlocks again in trial of former FCI Dublin officer
summary: A second jury failed to reach a verdict in the case against former officer Darrell Wayne Smith, who denied the allegations.

title: Judge rules New Hampshire may change how it settles YDC abuse claims
summary: A Merrimack County judge allowed the state to proceed with its revised settlement process despite survivors' objections. The judge said the Legislature had authority to change the rules.

title: Appeals delays leave Boy Scouts abuse survivors waiting on bulk of settlement payouts
summary: Bloomberg Law reported that continuing appeals were holding up full distributions from the survivor trust. Most insurer money remained in escrow pending final resolution of the challenges.

title: Federal court approves Rochester diocese settlement with survivors
summary: A federal bankruptcy court approved the Diocese of Rochester's settlement plan with abuse survivors.

title: Harrods moves to remove Egyptian Hall busts of Al Fayed
summary: Harrods applied for planning permission to remodel its Egyptian Hall, removing sculptures of its former owner after feedback from survivors.

title: House committee posts first batch of DOJ Epstein files
summary: The Oversight Committee publicly released records it received from the Justice Department, though most had already been public.

title: Syracuse diocese bankruptcy plan approved, awarding survivors $176 million
summary: A bankruptcy judge approved the Diocese of Syracuse's exit plan providing $176 million for abuse survivors.

title: House panel subpoenas Epstein estate for documents including 'birthday book'
summary: The House Oversight Committee subpoenaed Epstein's estate for records including a 2003 birthday album, contact books and financial documents.

title: Justice Department releases transcripts of Maxwell interviews
summary: The department published transcripts and audio of Maxwell's interviews, in which she denied witnessing misconduct by prominent figures.

title: Nearly 150 people report allegations against Al Fayed to police
summary: The Metropolitan Police said about 146 people had come forward since its new investigation began and that it was examining people who may have enabled the alleged abuse.

title: Two former FCI Dublin officers plead guilty to federal sex abuse charges
summary: The two most recently charged former officers pleaded guilty to sexually abusing incarcerated women.

title: House Oversight Committee subpoenas Epstein files and seeks Clinton depositions
summary: The House Oversight Committee subpoenaed the Justice Department for Epstein case files and sought depositions from Bill and Hillary Clinton and former law enforcement officials.

title: Ghislaine Maxwell moved to minimum-security prison camp in Texas
summary: The Bureau of Prisons transferred Maxwell from a Florida prison to a lower-security camp in Bryan, Texas, days after her Justice Department interviews.

title: Church nears global settlement in dozens of California abuse lawsuits
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: Filings indicated progress on a settlement in principle covering more than 100 California claims against the church.

title: Arizona appeals court revives Bisbee abuse lawsuit against church
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: An appeals court unanimously reversed the dismissal, finding the church may have had a duty to report and that clergy privilege has limits.

title: Survivors allege Pope Leo XIV covered up abuse reports in Peru
summary: Survivors from the Chiclayo diocese said their complaints were not properly handled while Prevost was bishop; the diocese and Vatican have said the case was processed correctly.

title: Rotherham survivors allege they were also abused by police officers
summary: Five women abused by Rotherham grooming gangs alleged they were also raped or sexually abused by South Yorkshire Police officers; the allegations are under review.

title: Maxwell given limited immunity in interviews with deputy attorney general
summary: Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche interviewed Maxwell over two days in Tallahassee under a grant of limited immunity.

title: More than 100 join Harrods redress scheme as it widens to Fayed's airline
summary: Over 100 people had registered for the Harrods scheme, which was extended to former staff of Al Fayed's private airline and runs until March 2026.

title: Judge denies request to unseal Florida Epstein grand jury transcripts
summary: A federal judge in Florida rejected the Justice Department's request to release transcripts from 2005-2007 grand jury proceedings, citing secrecy rules.

title: YDC fund administrator departs after new law shifts control to governor and AG
summary: Retired Chief Justice John Broderick left his post as YDC settlement fund administrator after a new law gave the attorney general veto power over awards. He disputed the governor's account that he resigned.

title: Jim Jordan deposed under oath in Strauss lawsuit
summary: Rep. Jim Jordan gave his first sworn testimony in the federal suits, maintaining he never saw or heard of abuse; former athletic director Andy Geiger was also deposed.

title: Excavation begins at Tuam mother and baby home site
summary: A full forensic excavation began at the former Tuam home, where remains of about 800 children are believed to be buried.

title: DOJ and FBI memo says no Epstein client list exists
summary: A Justice Department and FBI review concluded there was no evidence of a client list or blackmail scheme and affirmed Epstein died by suicide, sparking bipartisan backlash.

title: New charges against more FCI Dublin officers bring total charged to 10
summary: After federal prosecutors charged two more former officers, women who were held at Dublin spoke about the scale of abuse.

title: Combs acquitted of racketeering and sex trafficking, convicted on prostitution-related counts
summary: Jurors found Combs not guilty of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking but convicted him on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution under the Mann Act.

title: Judge denies Combs bail pending sentencing despite partial acquittal
summary: Judge Subramanian ordered Combs to stay jailed until sentencing, citing evidence of violence presented at trial.

title: Diocese of Fresno files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
summary: The Diocese of Fresno filed for bankruptcy protection to address abuse claims brought under California law.

title: About 3,880 abuse claims filed in rush to beat Maryland's new caps
summary: Thousands of claims were filed in the weeks before the June 1 cap change, with the Department of Juvenile Services facing the most allegations.

title: Jes Staley loses challenge to UK ban over Epstein statements
summary: A UK tribunal upheld the Financial Conduct Authority's finding that Staley misled regulators about his relationship with Epstein, keeping a ban on senior industry roles.

title: Supreme Court rejects R. Kelly's appeal of racketeering conviction
summary: The Supreme Court declined to review Kelly's New York racketeering and sex trafficking convictions, leaving his 30-year sentence intact.

title: Judge denies R. Kelly's bid for release over claimed prison safety threats
summary: A federal judge in Chicago rejected Kelly's emergency request for release or home confinement, which claimed prison officials were plotting against him.

title: Casey audit finds flawed data used to dismiss concerns about grooming gangs
summary: Baroness Casey's national audit found authorities shied away from examining offenders' ethnicity and relied on poor data; the government accepted all of her recommendations.

title: Ed Henry accuser settles sex-trafficking suit on eve of trial
summary: The former producer settled her claims against Henry one day before trial; her lawyers said they would appeal the dismissal of Fox News to the Second Circuit.

title: Prime minister announces national inquiry into grooming gangs
summary: Keir Starmer said a national statutory inquiry into grooming gangs would be set up, reversing his earlier position, ahead of publication of the Casey audit.

title: Rochdale grooming gang found guilty of raping and abusing two girls
summary: A jury convicted members of a Rochdale gang of raping and abusing two girls in the early 2000s following a long-running historical investigation.

title: Third Circuit declines to rehear challenge to Boy Scouts Chapter 11 plan
summary: The appeals court refused panel and en banc rehearing of its May ruling upholding the plan. Objecting claimants could next petition the Supreme Court.

title: Judge declares mistrial on remaining rape count in Weinstein retrial
summary: The judge declared a mistrial on the third-degree rape charge involving actress Jessica Mann after the jury foreperson refused to continue deliberating.

title: Retrial jury convicts Weinstein on one count, acquits on another
summary: A Manhattan jury convicted Weinstein of a first-degree criminal sexual act involving former production assistant Miriam Haley and acquitted him of a charge involving actress Kaja Sokola, continuing to deliberate on a rape count.

title: Seven clergy to face discipline over Smyth abuse failures
summary: An independent judge allowed seven of the ten complaints to proceed, while Carey and two others faced no further action.

title: Brand pleads not guilty at Southwark Crown Court; trial set for June 2026
summary: Brand entered not-guilty pleas to all five charges and a trial expected to last several weeks was scheduled for June 2026.

title: Michigan Senate passes bills extending time for abuse survivors to sue
summary: Citing the Nassar and Anderson scandals, the state Senate passed bills extending civil deadlines, opening a one-year lookback window and allowing suits against public universities.

title: Cassie Ventura testifies against Combs
summary: Ventura spent several days on the stand describing abuse and coercion during her relationship with Combs.

title: Third Circuit upholds Boy Scouts bankruptcy plan, saying it is too late to unwind
summary: The Third Circuit rejected appeals by a small group of claimants and holdout insurers, ruling the plan had been consummated too far to be reversed despite the Supreme Court's 2024 Purdue Pharma decision on third-party releases. The trust can keep paying about 82,000 claimants.

title: Opening statements begin in Sean Combs' federal trial
summary: Prosecutors and defense lawyers gave opening statements in Combs' racketeering and sex trafficking trial in Manhattan federal court.

title: Allegations resurface that new Pope Leo XIV mishandled abuse cases
summary: After Robert Prevost's election, survivor groups revived claims he failed to act on abuse reports in Chicago and Peru, which his former diocese denied.

title: Columbia and NewYork-Presbyterian reach $750 million Hadden settlement
summary: A $750 million settlement covering 576 cases pushed total civil payouts related to Hadden above $1 billion.

title: Brand makes first court appearance in London and is granted conditional bail
summary: Brand appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court, confirmed his details and was granted conditional bail, with the case sent to Southwark Crown Court. He denies all charges.

title: Pentagon report: military sexual assault reports fell 4% in fiscal 2024
summary: The annual report counted 8,195 reports in fiscal 2024, down from 8,515, with the Army posting the largest drop; officials warned staffing cuts could slow progress.

title: L.A. County supervisors approve record $4 billion juvenile sex abuse settlement
summary: The Board of Supervisors approved the $4 billion payout, described as the largest such settlement in U.S. history. The claims were brought under the state law that revived expired childhood abuse claims.

title: SafeSport CEO Ju'Riese Colon departs amid criticism of the center
summary: SafeSport announced that CEO Ju'Riese Colon was no longer leading the organization, with the board chair heading an interim committee. The change followed criticism over backlogs, case closures and the investigator arrest.

title: Weinstein's New York sex crimes retrial opens
summary: Opening statements began in Manhattan in Weinstein's retrial on charges involving three women, after the 2020 conviction was overturned.

title: Child Victims Act overhaul with lower caps signed into law
summary: The bill reducing damages for future claims became law, with court challenges expected.

title: Buffalo diocese reaches $150 million settlement with abuse survivors
summary: The Diocese of Buffalo agreed to a $150 million settlement with survivors in its bankruptcy case.

title: Documentary on Strauss scandal set for Tribeca premiere and HBO release
summary: The George Clooney-produced documentary Surviving Ohio State was scheduled to premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival before airing on HBO.

title: Moore rejects calls to veto Child Victims Act overhaul
summary: The governor declined survivors' calls for a veto as attorneys rushed to file cases before the lower caps took effect.

title: Jury awards $1.68 billion to 40 women who accused James Toback of sexual abuse
summary: A Manhattan civil jury found Toback liable and awarded about $1.68 billion in damages to 40 women in the Adult Survivors Act case; he did not participate in the trial.

title: New York judge refuses to pause Arthur lawsuit; Warner Bros offers film outtakes
summary: In the New York civil case brought by an Arthur extra, a judge rejected Brand's request to delay proceedings because of the UK criminal case, and Warner Bros Discovery said it held hours of outtake footage. Both defendants deny the claims.

title: Maryland lawmakers pass bill lowering damage caps on child sex abuse claims
summary: The General Assembly passed caps of $400,000 for claims against public institutions and $700,000 for private ones, for suits filed after June 1, 2025.

title: Prosecutors file superseding indictment adding charges against Combs
summary: A third superseding indictment added sex trafficking and Mann Act counts involving a second alleged victim, bringing the total to five counts.

title: Russell Brand charged with rape, oral rape, indecent assault and sexual assault
summary: The CPS authorised charges against Brand of one count of rape, one of oral rape, one of indecent assault and two of sexual assault, involving four women between 1999 and 2005. Brand denied the allegations and said he would defend himself in court.

title: L.A. County reaches tentative $4 billion settlement of more than 6,800 child sex abuse claims
summary: Los Angeles County tentatively agreed to pay $4 billion to resolve more than 6,800 claims of childhood sexual abuse, mostly tied to juvenile facilities and foster care. Officials called it the costliest settlement in county history.

title: Defrocked former cardinal Theodore McCarrick dies at 94 without facing trial
summary: McCarrick, the highest-ranking U.S. churchman to be dismissed from the priesthood over sexual abuse, died in Missouri at age 94. Both criminal cases against him had ended with findings that he was not competent to stand trial.

title: Federal judge dismisses most of Johnny Hunt's defamation claims against SBC and Guidepost
summary: A Tennessee federal judge ruled for the SBC, its Executive Committee and Guidepost on most claims, leaving one claim against former president Bart Barber.

title: Harrods launches compensation scheme offering up to £385,000
summary: Harrods opened a redress scheme for people alleging abuse by Al Fayed, offering up to £385,000 plus treatment costs; survivors' lawyers criticised the store's control of the process.

title: Attorney general's office says proposed abuse-claim changes not clearly unconstitutional
summary: The AG's office advised that the legislature's proposed limits on Child Victims Act damages could likely withstand challenge.

title: U.S. Supreme Court declines Steve Wynn's bid to revisit libel standard
summary: The Supreme Court turned away Steve Wynn's appeal in his defamation case against the AP, which had asked the justices to reconsider New York Times v. Sullivan.

title: Harrods proposes six-figure settlements to alleged Al Fayed victims
summary: Harrods set out proposed payouts for claimants, with higher awards linked to agreeing to a psychiatric assessment.

title: New Hampshire Supreme Court agrees to hear $38 million YDC verdict dispute
summary: The state's highest court accepted the case over whether the jury award should stand or be capped at $475,000.

title: Survivors rally as Maryland faces pressure to settle billions in abuse claims
summary: More than 100 people alleging abuse in state agencies rallied in Baltimore, urging state leaders to resolve their claims amid a budget deficit.

title: Robert Morris surrenders in Oklahoma, released on bond
summary: Morris was booked, released on $50,000 bond and entered a not guilty plea.

title: Justice Department closes SBC abuse investigation without new charges
summary: SBC leaders said the DOJ had concluded its probe of the convention with no charges against SBC entities.

title: Judge dismisses Fox News from sexual assault lawsuit against Ed Henry
summary: A federal judge ruled Fox lacked notice of Henry's alleged conduct before 2020 and dismissed the network from the suit, leaving claims against Henry for trial.

title: Robert Morris indicted by Oklahoma grand jury on child sex abuse charges
summary: An Osage County grand jury indicted Morris on five counts of lewd or indecent acts with a child.

title: SBC leaders cite mounting legal bills from abuse-related litigation
summary: The Executive Committee reported strained finances driven by legal costs from the abuse investigation and related lawsuits.

title: Former SafeSport investigator charged with rape and trafficking from police tenure
summary: Jason Krasley, a former Allentown, Pennsylvania officer hired by SafeSport as an investigator, was charged with rape and sex trafficking offenses tied to his police work, raising questions about the center's hiring. SafeSport had dismissed him in late 2024.

title: Judge grants final approval of consent decree in FCI Dublin class action
summary: A federal judge approved a two-year consent decree in the class action brought by former Dublin residents, providing monitoring and protections at women's prisons.

title: Justice Department's first Epstein files release yields few new revelations
summary: Attorney General Pam Bondi's office released a first batch of Epstein-related records, much of which had already been public.

title: Former Archbishop George Carey among clergy facing disciplinary review over Smyth
summary: The National Safeguarding Team sought permission to bring out-of-time disciplinary cases against ten clergy named in the review.

title: Eighty more patients sue Columbia and affiliates over Hadden
summary: Another 80 former patients filed suit against Columbia and affiliated institutions over Hadden's abuse.

title: Maryland faces about $3 billion exposure from abuse claims under 2023 law
summary: Legislative documents showed roughly 3,500 suits against the state and potential liability of about $3.11 billion. A bill to reinstate a filing deadline was being rewritten.

title: Abuse database no longer a priority for SBC leaders
summary: SBC executives said legal and financial hurdles had derailed the planned database of accused ministers.

title: Suit accusing Combs and Jay-Z of assaulting a 13-year-old is dismissed
summary: An anonymous plaintiff represented by Buzbee voluntarily dismissed her suit against Combs and Shawn 'Jay-Z' Carter, both of whom denied the allegations.

title: Federal appeals court upholds R. Kelly's racketeering conviction and 30-year term
summary: The 2nd Circuit affirmed Kelly's New York racketeering and sex trafficking convictions and his 30-year sentence.

title: General Synod repents of safeguarding failures after Makin Review
summary: The Synod approved a motion acknowledging failures and committing to strengthen safeguarding practice.

title: Report details 17 cases of abuse by IHOPKC founder Mike Bickle
institution: International House of Prayer Kansas City (IHOPKC)
summary: An investigative report found Bickle abused 17 women and girls and that staff protected him.

title: Maryland lawmakers weigh limiting state liability under Child Victims Act
summary: Senate leaders said they would consider changes to reduce the state's exposure after the court upheld the law.

title: Maryland Supreme Court upholds Child Victims Act in 4-3 ruling
summary: The court held the 2017 limit was an ordinary statute of limitations the Legislature could repeal, allowing revived claims to proceed.

title: Philadelphia congregation member sentenced in grand jury abuse case
summary: David Balosa received two to four years in prison after a jury convicted him of assaulting a child in 1998.

title: Redress scheme compensates two men over abuse attributed to Pell
summary: Australia's National Redress Scheme, created after the royal commission, granted compensation to two men who said Pell abused them in Ballarat in the 1970s; the scheme is not a court finding.

title: BBC review finds staff felt unable to complain about Brand; corporation apologises
summary: A BBC review of Brand's 2006-2008 tenure at Radio 2 and 6 Music examined eight complaints, found the only formal one at the time was handled ineffectively and that compliance checks failed, and concluded staff felt unable to speak up. The BBC apologised to those affected.

title: Former YDC supervisor Bradley Asbury sentenced to at least 20 years
summary: A judge sentenced Asbury to at least 20 years in prison for his role in the 1998 assault of a resident. Separately, former worker Stanley Watson was convicted that month.

title: Legislators warned of enormous liability from thousands of abuse suits against the state
summary: Analysts told lawmakers that about 3,500 suits had been filed against state agencies, mainly the Department of Juvenile Services, with potential costs in the billions.

title: Pope Francis dissolves Peru's Sodalitium movement
summary: The Vatican moved to suppress the Sodalitium Christianae Vitae after the investigation documented widespread abuses.

title: UK government announces local inquiries and national audit on grooming gangs
summary: Home Secretary Yvette Cooper announced a rapid national audit led by Baroness Casey and funding for local inquiries, after weeks of political pressure over grooming gangs.

title: Government pledges to introduce mandatory reporting of child sexual abuse
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The government said it would legislate for mandatory reporting and act on other IICSA recommendations amid renewed political pressure over child sexual abuse.

title: Police watchdog oversees probe into Met's handling of 2008 Al Fayed complaints
summary: The Independent Office for Police Conduct began overseeing an investigation into how the Metropolitan Police dealt with complaints against Al Fayed in 2008.

title: Court allows disputed YDC verdict to go to New Hampshire Supreme Court
summary: A Superior Court judge approved sending the dispute over the $38 million verdict and the state's damages cap to the state Supreme Court.

title: Michigan AG report names 56 clergy in Diocese of Lansing
summary: The fourth report in Michigan's statewide inquiry identified 56 clergy and religious accused of abuse in the Diocese of Lansing.

title: U.S. agrees to pay nearly $116 million to settle FCI Dublin abuse lawsuits
summary: The federal government agreed to pay about $116 million to 103 women who said they were sexually abused at Dublin.

title: Judge denies Sean Combs bail for a third time
summary: Judge Arun Subramanian rejected Combs' $50 million bail package, citing concerns about witness tampering.

title: Former YDC staffer Bradley Asbury convicted as accomplice in 1998 rape
summary: A jury convicted former YDC house leader Bradley Asbury on two counts of accomplice to aggravated felonious sexual assault. He became the first former staffer convicted in the scandal.

title: Plaintiff appeals cap on $38 million YDC verdict to New Hampshire Supreme Court
summary: The plaintiff in the landmark YDC verdict asked the state Supreme Court to overturn a ruling capping his award at $475,000.

title: Archbishop of Canterbury Justin Welby resigns over Smyth case
summary: Welby resigned, saying he took personal responsibility for failures identified by the Makin Review.

title: Carol Folt, hired after Tyndall scandal, to retire as USC president
summary: Folt announced her retirement, with her tenure credited with addressing the Tyndall-era scandals but criticized over other campus issues.

title: Makin Review finds Church of England covered up John Smyth's abuse
summary: The independent review concluded church officials knew of Smyth's abuse for decades and failed to report it, including after Archbishop Justin Welby was informed in 2013.

title: Met passes evidence file on Brand to prosecutors for charging decision
summary: The Crown Prosecution Service confirmed it had received a file of evidence from the Metropolitan Police, which had interviewed Brand three times, and was considering whether to bring charges. Brand denied the allegations.

title: Gateway Church removes elders after investigation into Morris case
summary: Following a law firm investigation, Gateway dismissed several elders who knew of the accusations.

title: Harrods says it is settling more than 250 claims
summary: Harrods said it was in the process of settling over 250 claims from people alleging abuse by its former owner and was reviewing whether any current staff were involved.

title: Supreme Court declines to hear R. Kelly's appeal of Chicago convictions
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court turned away Kelly's challenge to his child pornography and enticement convictions, which argued the charges were time-barred.

title: Attorney says 120 people plan to sue Combs alleging sexual misconduct
summary: Houston lawyer Tony Buzbee said 120 people had come forward with allegations against Combs and that dozens of suits would follow. Combs denied the claims.

title: Rockville Centre diocese agrees to pay $323 million to abuse survivors
summary: The Diocese of Rockville Centre reached a $323 million deal with survivors, among the largest Catholic bankruptcy settlements.

title: Pope expels a bishop and nine others from Sodalitium over abuses
summary: Francis expelled ten members, including a retired archbishop, citing physical and sadistic abuse and abuse of power.

title: Wynn Resorts agrees to $70 million settlement of investor class action
summary: Wynn Resorts agreed to pay $70 million to settle a securities class action alleging it misled investors about the misconduct allegations against its founder, closing a major remaining legal chapter.

title: Dozens of women accuse Al Fayed; Harrods apologises
summary: Lawyers said 37 women had made allegations against Al Fayed, who died in 2023, and the store's current owners apologised for failing employees.

title: BBC investigation alleges Mohamed Al Fayed raped and assaulted Harrods staff
summary: A BBC documentary and podcast reported allegations from former female employees that the late Harrods owner sexually assaulted or raped them, and that the company failed to intervene.

title: Sean Combs arrested and indicted on sex trafficking and racketeering charges
summary: Federal prosecutors in Manhattan unsealed an indictment charging Combs with racketeering conspiracy, sex trafficking and Mann Act transportation; he pleaded not guilty and was denied bail.

title: Appeals court upholds Ghislaine Maxwell's conviction
summary: The 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected Maxwell's argument that Epstein's 2008 non-prosecution agreement shielded her from prosecution.

title: Huw Edwards given suspended six-month sentence
summary: Edwards received a six-month prison sentence suspended for two years and was ordered to attend a sex offender treatment programme.

title: Weinstein indicted on additional sex crime charges ahead of New York retrial
summary: A Manhattan grand jury indicted Weinstein on a new criminal sexual act charge involving a third woman, to be tried alongside the retried counts.

title: Nevada Supreme Court ends Steve Wynn's defamation suit against the AP
summary: Nevada's high court upheld dismissal of Steve Wynn's defamation lawsuit over an Associated Press report on police complaints against him, finding the reporting protected.

title: UK prosecutors drop indecent assault case against Weinstein
summary: The Crown Prosecution Service discontinued the London indecent assault charges, saying there was no longer a realistic prospect of conviction.

title: Mistrial declared after jury deadlocks in first YDC criminal case
summary: A judge declared a mistrial after jurors could not reach a verdict in the case against former youth center worker Victor Malavet.

title: First criminal trial in YDC abuse scandal begins
summary: Former youth center worker Victor Malavet went on trial on charges of sexually assaulting a teenage resident in the early 2000s, the first criminal trial arising from the scandal. He denied the charges.

title: Vatican expels Sodalitium founder Figari
summary: Following the investigation, the Vatican expelled Figari from the movement over abuses including sexual abuse.

title: Huw Edwards pleads guilty to indecent image charges
summary: Edwards pleaded guilty at Westminster Magistrates' Court to three charges of making indecent images of children; the BBC said it would seek to recover pay from him.

title: Former BBC newsreader Huw Edwards charged with making indecent images of children
summary: Huw Edwards, who had resigned from the BBC in April 2024, was charged with three counts of making indecent images of children.

title: YDC settlement fund claims surpass 500
summary: More than 500 claims had been filed with the YDC settlement fund after eligibility expanded, with many more expected before the deadline.

title: $104 million awarded to Mount Cashel survivors and victims of N.L. priests
summary: About $104 million from the Archdiocese of St. John's insolvency process was allocated to people abused at Mount Cashel and by Newfoundland priests.

title: Second Kanakuk abuse survivor sues camp alleging fraudulent concealment
summary: Another man abused by Pete Newman sued Kanakuk, current and former leaders and its insurer, alleging they concealed knowledge of Newman's behavior. Kanakuk maintained Newman was a rogue employee.

title: Gateway Church founder Robert Morris resigns over child abuse allegation
summary: Morris stepped down days after a woman publicly said he abused her beginning in 1982 when she was a child.

title: Diocese of San Diego files for bankruptcy for second time
summary: Facing about 450 new abuse claims, the Diocese of San Diego filed for Chapter 11 protection again.

title: Banijay UK investigation finds concerns about Brand on Endemol shows were not escalated
summary: An investigation by law firm Lewis Silkin found informal concerns about Brand's conduct on Endemol-produced Channel 4 shows reached senior staff but were not escalated or adequately addressed, and that Endemol lacked clear escalation routes and conduct training.

title: New Hampshire expands YDC fund eligibility and raises settlement caps
summary: The state broadened the types of abuse eligible for YDC fund payments and raised caps in a bid to steer victims away from lawsuits. The changes followed low early participation in the fund.

title: Future of SBC abuse reform handed to denominational committee
summary: At the Indianapolis meeting the task force concluded its work, leaving reforms to the Executive Committee.

title: Howard University revokes Combs' honorary degree and cuts ties
summary: Howard's trustees rescinded Combs' 2014 honorary doctorate, returned his donation and ended a scholarship agreement after the hotel video.

title: Former elder convicted of abusing three children in Lancaster County
summary: A jury convicted Norman Aviles-Garriga on all 12 counts in a case brought from the grand jury investigation.

title: Combs apologizes after video shows him assaulting Cassie in 2016
summary: After CNN aired 2016 hotel surveillance footage showing Combs attacking Ventura, he posted a video apology calling his actions inexcusable.

title: Boy Scouts of America announces name change to Scouting America
summary: The organization announced it would rebrand as Scouting America in 2025, a change that followed years of declining membership and the abuse-driven bankruptcy.

title: Maryland Supreme Court agrees to decide Child Victims Act's constitutionality
summary: The state's highest court took up the challenge to the law that allowed decades-old abuse claims.

title: Jurors dispute state's bid to cap $38 million YDC verdict at $475,000
summary: Jurors said the state misread their verdict after it argued a $475,000 statutory cap applied because the jury found a single incident. The cap dispute became the central fight over the award.

title: Jury finds New Hampshire liable for youth center abuse, awards $38 million
summary: A jury found the state liable in the landmark first YDC civil trial and awarded the plaintiff $38 million. The state quickly signaled it would seek to limit the payment.

title: Louisiana probe of New Orleans clergy abuse expands to church leaders
summary: Louisiana State Police executed a search warrant at the Archdiocese of New Orleans as the investigation widened to senior officials suspected of shielding abusers.

title: Dan Schneider sues 'Quiet on Set' producers for defamation
summary: Schneider sued Warner Bros. Discovery, Sony and the docuseries producers, alleging the series falsely implied he sexually abused children.

title: Appeals court upholds R. Kelly's 20-year Chicago sentence
summary: The 7th Circuit rejected Kelly's argument that the statute of limitations barred his prosecution and affirmed his Chicago convictions and sentence.

title: New York's highest court overturns Weinstein's 2020 rape conviction
summary: The New York Court of Appeals ruled 4-3 that the trial judge improperly allowed testimony about uncharged allegations, vacating Weinstein's conviction and ordering a new trial.

title: Justice Department agrees to $138.7 million settlement over FBI's Nassar failures
summary: The Justice Department agreed to pay $138.7 million to resolve claims from 139 people who said the FBI's failure to act on 2015 reports allowed Nassar's abuse to continue.

title: Bureau of Prisons to close FCI Dublin after sexual abuse scandal
summary: The BOP announced it would shut the women's prison and transfer its incarcerated population to other facilities.

title: First civil trial over abuse at New Hampshire youth center opens
summary: The first of more than 1,100 lawsuits over abuse at the Youth Development Center went to trial in Brentwood. The former resident who brought the case alleged repeated abuse by staff in the 1990s.

title: SafeSport announces operational changes after congressional criticism
summary: Following a Senate hearing and a commission finding that it had lost athletes' trust, SafeSport unveiled 10 changes including a dedicated team for cases involving minors and more time for claimants to respond to evidence.

title: Diocese of Sacramento files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
summary: The Diocese of Sacramento filed for bankruptcy protection, citing more than 250 abuse claims under California's lookback window.

title: Montgomery County judge finds Child Victims Act unconstitutional
summary: A second circuit judge ruled the law violated the Maryland Declaration of Rights, creating conflicting rulings for the state's top court to resolve.

title: Federal agents raid Sean Combs' homes in Los Angeles and Miami
summary: Homeland Security Investigations agents searched Combs' properties as part of a federal sex trafficking investigation; his lawyer called it a witch hunt.

title: Channel 4 review finds 2009 complaint against Brand was not escalated; CEO apologises
summary: Channel 4's internal review found no evidence staff knew of the Dispatches allegations beforehand, but chief executive Alex Mahon apologised to a former employee whose serious 2009 complaint about Brand was neither escalated nor properly investigated.

title: Former Nickelodeon producer Dan Schneider apologizes after 'Quiet on Set' backlash
summary: Schneider released a video apologizing for some workplace behavior depicted in the series while not admitting to sexual misconduct.

title: Judge will appoint special master to oversee FCI Dublin
summary: A federal judge said she would appoint a special master to oversee the prison, an unprecedented step for a federal Bureau of Prisons facility.

title: FBI agents search FCI Dublin amid ongoing abuse investigation
summary: FBI agents searched the prison and seized devices and records, as the facility faced dozens of lawsuits and leadership was removed.

title: Drake Bell to reveal childhood abuse by Nickelodeon dialogue coach in 'Quiet on Set'
summary: Former Nickelodeon star Drake Bell said he would publicly identify himself as the victim of dialogue coach Brian Peck, convicted in 2004, in the docuseries examining alleged toxic conditions on Nickelodeon sets.

title: Prince George's judge rules Child Victims Act constitutional
summary: A circuit judge upheld the law against a constitutional challenge brought by the Archdiocese of Washington.

title: Strauss plaintiffs say case could head to trial as judge encourages mediation
summary: At a status conference, attorneys for remaining plaintiffs said the case could go to trial in 2025 while the judge pushed for mediation.

title: Utah Legislature expands clergy ability to report child abuse
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: Utah lawmakers passed a bill shielding clergy from liability when they report abuse learned in confession.

title: Producer sues Combs alleging sexual harassment and assault
summary: Producer Rodney 'Lil Rod' Jones, who worked on Combs' 2023 album, filed suit alleging sexual harassment, assault and illegal activity. Combs' lawyers denied the claims.

title: Supreme Court declines to pause Boy Scouts bankruptcy plan during appeals
summary: The Supreme Court, without noted dissent, denied a request by a group of abuse claimants to stay the Boy Scouts plan while their challenge proceeded in the Third Circuit.

title: SBC abuse task force plans new nonprofit to run database and reforms
summary: The implementation task force proposed spinning off an independent nonprofit to oversee the accused-minister database.

title: Les Moonves to pay Los Angeles ethics fine over interference in police probe
summary: Les Moonves agreed to pay $11,250 to resolve a Los Angeles Ethics Commission complaint that he induced a retired LAPD captain to share confidential details of a 2017 sexual assault report against him.

title: Bickle accused of abusing a 14-year-old before IHOPKC's founding
institution: International House of Prayer Kansas City (IHOPKC)
summary: A new allegation involving a minor in the 1980s emerged as IHOPKC released investigation findings.

title: Criminal case against Tyndall formally dismissed after his death
summary: A judge dismissed the criminal case against Tyndall following his death, ending the prosecution without a verdict.

title: Review finds police and council left Rochdale children at mercy of gangs
summary: An independent review commissioned by Mayor Andy Burnham found Greater Manchester Police and Rochdale council failed to protect girls in the 2000s and identified 96 men still thought to pose a risk.

title: Hollywood Commission finds culture shift but weak accountability seven years after Weinstein
summary: A new Hollywood Commission survey found workers more aware of harassment and reporting options but still skeptical that powerful offenders face consequences.

title: Wisconsin judge suspends criminal case against McCarrick, finding him unfit for trial
summary: A Walworth County judge suspended McCarrick's sexual assault case after ruling he was mentally incompetent to stand trial and unlikely to regain competency, mirroring the earlier Massachusetts outcome.

title: Michigan attorney general releases second report on clergy abuse
summary: Attorney General Dana Nessel issued the second in a series of diocese-by-diocese reports from her statewide investigation of clergy abuse.

title: Court documents naming Epstein associates unsealed
summary: A federal judge's order led to the release of hundreds of pages from Giuffre's defamation case against Maxwell naming people connected to Epstein; being named did not imply wrongdoing.

title: Medical examiner attributes Tyndall's death to natural causes
summary: The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner reported that Tyndall died of cardiovascular disease.

title: Southern Baptists settle abuse lawsuit tied to Paul Pressler
summary: SBC entities reached a settlement in a long-running Texas lawsuit alleging abuse by former judge and SBC leader Paul Pressler, who denied the claims.

title: Bobby Kotick to leave Activision Blizzard after Microsoft takeover
summary: Microsoft confirmed CEO Bobby Kotick would depart on Dec. 29, 2023, following its acquisition of the company.

title: Brand questioned again by London police over six further alleged offences
summary: UK media reported that Brand was interviewed a second time by Metropolitan Police officers, this time about six more alleged sexual offences. He continued to deny all wrongdoing.

title: MSU trustees vote to release Nassar documents to the attorney general
summary: Michigan State's board voted to waive privilege and release thousands of Nassar-related documents to the attorney general's office after years of pressure from survivors.

title: Activision Blizzard to pay $54 million to settle California civil rights lawsuit
summary: The company agreed to pay $54 million to resolve the state's lawsuit, mostly over pay and promotion claims; the settlement stated no court or independent investigation had substantiated claims of systemic sexual harassment.

title: IHOPKC cuts ties with Mike Bickle
institution: International House of Prayer Kansas City (IHOPKC)
summary: IHOPKC announced its permanent separation from its founder, citing the level of inappropriate behavior uncovered.

title: Mike Bickle admits unspecified past moral failures
institution: International House of Prayer Kansas City (IHOPKC)
summary: Bickle acknowledged inappropriate behavior years earlier but did not address the specific abuse allegations.

title: New competency exam leaves McCarrick's Wisconsin sexual assault case in doubt
summary: A state psychologist's evaluation of McCarrick, charged in Walworth County, Wisconsin, with a 1977 sexual assault at a lake resort, raised doubts about whether the case could proceed to trial.

title: Recordings show how church handled abuse claims against former bishop
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: AP reported recordings in which church officials discouraged a bishop from testifying and offered a confidential settlement in a case involving a former bishop.

title: Former FCI Dublin officer John Bellhouse sentenced to over five years
summary: Bellhouse, convicted by a jury in June of sexually abusing two incarcerated women, was sentenced to five years and three months.

title: Combs steps down as Revolt chairman amid abuse lawsuits
summary: Combs stepped aside as chairman of Revolt Media & TV as civil suits accusing him of sexual abuse mounted.

title: Two more women sue Sean Combs alleging sexual abuse
summary: Two additional women filed suits accusing Combs of sexual assault in the early 1990s, just before New York's Adult Survivors Act window closed. Combs denied the claims.

title: Former Mount Cashel Christian Brother Edward English arrested in Vancouver
summary: Vancouver police arrested Edward English, previously convicted over Mount Cashel abuse, on new allegations stemming from his time at a Vancouver school.

title: Wave of celebrity abuse lawsuits filed before Adult Survivors Act window closes
summary: Lawsuits against entertainment figures including Axl Rose and Jamie Foxx were filed as New York's one-year lookback window expired; the defendants denied the claims.

title: Brand reportedly interviewed under caution by police over three non-recent sexual offences
summary: The Metropolitan Police said a man in his 40s, reported to be Brand, was interviewed under caution about three alleged non-recent sexual offences. He was not arrested.

title: Combs and Cassie settle her lawsuit one day after filing
summary: Combs and Ventura announced a confidential settlement a day after her suit was filed; Combs continued to deny wrongdoing.

title: Cassie Ventura sues Sean Combs alleging rape and years of abuse
summary: Singer Cassie Ventura, Combs' former girlfriend and Bad Boy artist, filed a federal suit accusing him of rape, physical abuse and sex trafficking over about a decade. Combs denied the allegations.

title: Former FCI Dublin officer sentenced to eight years as investigation continues
summary: A former correctional officer received an eight-year sentence for sexually abusing women at Dublin, one of several staff convicted.

title: BBC says two more people have come forward with complaints about Brand
summary: The BBC told MPs its review had received two further complaints about Brand's behaviour during his time at the corporation, and that the information had been passed to police.

title: Columbia announces $100 million fund and notification of 6,500 Hadden patients
summary: Columbia said it would create a $100 million survivors fund, notify about 6,500 former patients, and commission an external investigation.

title: Court dismisses Bisbee abuse lawsuit against church citing clergy-penitent privilege
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: An Arizona judge dismissed the lawsuit, finding bishops had no duty to report information learned in confession.

title: IHOPKC addresses investigation into abuse allegations against founder Mike Bickle
institution: International House of Prayer Kansas City (IHOPKC)
summary: IHOPKC discussed its third-party investigation after allegations of clergy sexual abuse against Bickle surfaced.

title: Film extra sues Brand and Warner Bros in New York over alleged assault on Arthur set
summary: An anonymous extra filed suit in New York State Supreme Court alleging Brand exposed himself and sexually assaulted her in a bathroom during the 2010 filming of Arthur; Warner Bros and production companies were also named as defendants. The defendants deny the allegations.

title: Nine months in, YDC settlement fund has resolved 29 claims for $13.4 million
summary: The state's YDC settlement fund had resolved 29 claims for about $13.4 million, with roughly 148 pending. Many victims continued to pursue lawsuits instead.

title: Facing more lawsuits, Ohio State denies covering up Strauss abuse
summary: With five lawsuits from more than 230 men pending, Ohio State denied a cover-up and argued the claims were time-barred.

title: Columbia apologizes as it confronts revelations about Hadden
summary: Columbia leadership issued an apology to Hadden's victims amid pressure from students, faculty and survivors following ProPublica's reporting.

title: Former Ohio State wrestlers oppose Jim Jordan's bid for House speaker
summary: Former wrestlers said Jordan was unfit to be speaker because of what they allege he knew about Strauss; Jordan denies the claims.

title: George Tyndall found dead at home while awaiting trial
summary: Tyndall, 76, was found dead at his Los Angeles home before his criminal trial, leaving the charges unresolved.

title: Julia Ormond sues Weinstein, accusing CAA, Disney and Miramax of enabling him
summary: Actress Julia Ormond filed a lawsuit under New York's Adult Survivors Act alleging Weinstein assaulted her in 1995 and that her agency CAA, Disney and Miramax failed to protect her.

title: Hadden faces hundreds of new abuse claims
summary: USA Today reported that hundreds of additional former patients had brought new abuse claims involving Hadden and Columbia.

title: Abuse suits under Maryland's new law, including against juvenile justice system, begin to stack up
summary: As the law took effect Oct. 1, lawsuits were filed against the state's juvenile justice system, schools and the Catholic Church.

title: Archdiocese of Baltimore files for bankruptcy ahead of expected lawsuits
summary: The Archdiocese of Baltimore filed for Chapter 11 two days before Maryland's Child Victims Act took effect.

title: JPMorgan settles U.S. Virgin Islands Epstein suit for $75 million
summary: JPMorgan agreed to pay $75 million to settle the territory's lawsuit, with funds earmarked in part for anti-trafficking efforts.

title: Metropolitan Police opens investigation into several non-recent sexual offence allegations
summary: The Met confirmed it had received a number of allegations of non-recent sexual offences in London and elsewhere following the media investigation and had launched an inquiry. No arrests had been made and Brand denied the allegations.

title: Channel 4 investigating Brand's time at the channel; says no evidence so far of complaints reaching management
summary: Channel 4 chief executive Alex Mahon said the broadcaster's internal investigation had so far found no evidence that alleged incidents were reported to management at the time, as Channel 4 and the BBC pulled Brand's content from their platforms.

title: YouTube suspends Russell Brand's channel from earning ad revenue
summary: YouTube suspended monetisation on Brand's channel, which had millions of subscribers, citing its creator responsibility policy after the allegations surfaced. Brand continued to deny wrongdoing.

title: BBC launches review of Brand's time at the corporation and removes some of his content
summary: The BBC announced a review of complaints about Brand's conduct while he presented on Radio 2 and 6 Music between 2006 and 2008, and removed some of his programmes from iPlayer and BBC Sounds.

title: Scotland Yard receives report of alleged 2003 sexual assault in Soho after Brand reporting
