summary: The Metropolitan Police said it received a report of a sexual assault allegedly committed in Soho in 2003, following the Times and Dispatches investigation, and urged other potential victims to come forward. Channel 4 had also opened an internal investigation and removed Brand's content from its streaming service.

title: Banijay UK opens urgent internal investigation into Brand's conduct on Endemol shows
summary: Banijay UK, which owns Endemol, the producer of Big Brother's Big Mouth and other shows Brand hosted, announced an urgent internal investigation into the allegations of misconduct.

title: Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4 Dispatches report rape and sexual assault allegations against Russell Brand
summary: A joint investigation by The Times, The Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches published allegations from four women of rape, sexual assault and emotional abuse between 2006 and 2013, during Brand's period as a star of BBC and Channel 4 programming. Brand denied the allegations, saying his relationships were consensual.

title: ProPublica: Columbia ignored warnings and protected Hadden for two decades
summary: A ProPublica and New York Magazine investigation detailed how Columbia failed to act on complaints and let Hadden return to work after his 2012 arrest.

title: Wynn Resorts settles suit by salon workers over failure to act on harassment
summary: Wynn Resorts reached a settlement with nine women who worked in its Las Vegas salon and alleged the company ignored complaints about Steve Wynn's conduct.

title: Danny Masterson sentenced to 30 years to life in prison
summary: A Los Angeles judge sentenced Danny Masterson to 30 years to life for two rape convictions after victims gave impact statements in court.

title: Congressional commission draft calls SafeSport 'in potential crisis'
summary: A draft report from the commission reviewing the U.S. Olympic system said feedback about the U.S. Center for SafeSport depicted an agency in potential crisis.

title: Massachusetts judge dismisses McCarrick sex abuse case after finding him not competent for trial
summary: A Dedham judge dismissed the criminal case against McCarrick, 93, after a prosecution expert agreed with the defense that dementia left him unable to assist in his own defense.

title: Tyndall pleads not guilty to 27 felony counts ahead of trial
summary: Tyndall entered not-guilty pleas to 18 counts of sexual penetration and nine counts of sexual battery remaining in the case.

title: Judge orders R. Kelly's music royalties paid to victims
summary: A federal judge ordered more than $500,000 in Kelly's royalties held by Universal Music Group turned over toward restitution for his victims.

title: Archdiocese of San Francisco files for bankruptcy
summary: The Archdiocese of San Francisco filed for Chapter 11 protection to pursue a global settlement of more than 500 abuse claims.

title: Five men convicted of historical child sex offences in Rochdale
summary: Five men were convicted of historical sexual offences against girls in Rochdale under Greater Manchester Police's Operation Lytton.

title: Brian Houston acquitted of concealing father's child sex abuse
summary: A Sydney magistrate found Houston not guilty, ruling he had a reasonable excuse for not reporting.

title: Tyndall ordered to stand trial on sexual assault charges
summary: After a preliminary hearing, a judge ruled there was sufficient evidence for Tyndall to stand trial on charges involving 16 patients.

title: UK Charity Commission closes nine-year inquiry into Watch Tower safeguarding
summary: The regulator said Watch Tower's legal challenges constrained its inquiry and found it had not been as transparent as it should have been.

title: Nassar survivors sue Michigan State over withheld documents
summary: Survivors sued MSU alleging trustees held secret votes on whether to release about 6,000 Nassar-related documents, in violation of open meetings and records laws.

title: Biden executive order shifts serious military crimes to independent prosecutors
summary: An executive order implemented the transfer of prosecution decisions for sexual assault and other serious crimes from commanders to special trial counsel offices due by year's end.

title: AP: SafeSport center overwhelmed six years after its creation
summary: An AP examination found SafeSport carried about 1,000 open cases with roughly 60 investigators, and that fewer than 15% of cases since 2017 reached formal resolution. Its leaders said funding was inadequate.

title: Kevin Spacey acquitted on all sexual offense charges in London
summary: A Southwark Crown Court jury found Kevin Spacey not guilty of nine sexual offense charges brought by four men dating to 2001-2013.

title: Hadden sentenced to 20 years in federal prison
summary: A federal judge sentenced Hadden to 20 years in prison for his conviction on enticement charges.

title: Steve Wynn agrees to pay $10 million to settle Nevada gaming complaint
summary: Steve Wynn agreed to a $10 million fine and to permanently exit the Nevada gaming industry to resolve a 2019 regulatory complaint, without admitting the allegations.

title: Vatican investigators begin audit of Peru's Sodalitium
summary: Archbishop Charles Scicluna and Msgr. Jordi Bertomeu opened a Vatican inquiry into abuse and financial allegations in Lima.

title: Pennsylvania authorities charge five more in Jehovah's Witnesses abuse probe
summary: The attorney general's office filed charges against five additional current or former members.

title: Nassar stabbed by another inmate in federal prison
summary: Nassar was stabbed multiple times by another inmate at a federal prison in Florida and was hospitalized in stable condition.

title: Judge denies Sandusky's latest request for a new trial
summary: A judge rejected Sandusky's petition, which argued new evidence undermined testimony based on recovered memories.

title: Fox pays $12 million to settle ex-producer's suit alleging sexism on Tucker Carlson show
summary: Fox settled for $12 million a former producer's suits alleging a misogynistic, hostile workplace on Tucker Carlson's show and coercion in the Dominion case.

title: Inspector general finds misconduct and failures at jail where Epstein died
summary: The Justice Department's inspector general found negligence, misconduct and job failures by Bureau of Prisons staff enabled Epstein's suicide, but no evidence of foul play.

title: Supreme Court declines Ohio State appeal, letting Strauss suits proceed
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear Ohio State's appeal, leaving in place the ruling that allowed the lawsuits to go forward.

title: Nearly 600 former detainees have sued L.A. County; county warns of up to $3 billion exposure
summary: Lawsuits on behalf of nearly 600 people allege sexual abuse in county juvenile facilities between 1972 and 2022. The county's chief executive estimated potential payouts of $1.6 billion to $3 billion across related claims.

title: Nine more women sue Cosby in Nevada under new law lifting time limits
summary: Nine women filed a federal lawsuit in Las Vegas alleging Cosby drugged and assaulted them decades ago, after Nevada eliminated the statute of limitations for such civil claims. Cosby's spokesman denied the allegations.

title: New complaint adds dozens more abuse allegations at L.A. County juvenile halls
summary: A new complaint filed in Los Angeles Superior Court alleges sexual abuse and other misconduct in county juvenile facilities from the 1970s through 2023. The filing firm said it represents more than 500 people.

title: JPMorgan Chase agrees to $290 million settlement with Epstein survivors
summary: JPMorgan reached a $290 million settlement with a class of Epstein survivors who said the bank enabled his abuse, without admitting liability.

title: Danny Masterson convicted of two counts of rape at retrial
summary: A Los Angeles jury convicted Danny Masterson of raping two women and deadlocked on a third count. He was taken into custody.

title: Inquiry chair and survivors dismayed by government response
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The government accepted the need for mandatory reporting and a redress scheme in principle, but Alexis Jay and survivors criticised the response as falling short.

title: Illinois attorney general finds 451 Catholic clergy abused nearly 2,000 children
summary: A nearly five-year investigation by Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul identified 451 Catholic clergy and lay employees who abused 1,997 children in the state's six dioceses since 1950, far more than the church had publicly acknowledged.

title: Deutsche Bank agrees to pay $75 million to Epstein survivors
summary: Deutsche Bank agreed to a $75 million settlement of a class action alleging it benefited from Epstein's sex trafficking, without admitting wrongdoing.

title: Diocese of Oakland files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
summary: The Diocese of Oakland, facing about 330 abuse lawsuits under California's window, filed for bankruptcy protection.

title: Dutch prosecutors to try Jehovah's Witness member on decades-old abuse charges
summary: Prosecutors charged a member over alleged abuse in the 1990s, following a 2018 raid on church offices and a legal fight over internal records.

title: California jury awards $2.3 billion in abuse case that had named the church
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: A Riverside County, California jury awarded $2.28 billion against an abuser; the church had earlier settled its part of the suit for $1 million while denying wrongdoing.

title: Heaps sentenced to 11 years in prison
summary: A judge sentenced Heaps to 11 years in state prison and ordered him to register as a sex offender.

title: Boy Scouts bankruptcy plan takes effect, creating survivor settlement trust
summary: The Boy Scouts emerged from Chapter 11 as its reorganization plan became effective, transferring assets and insurance rights to the Scouting Settlement Trust that pays abuse claims. Appeals by objectors remained pending.

title: More charges put focus on Jehovah's Witnesses' handling of abuse
summary: New grand jury charges in Pennsylvania renewed scrutiny of elders' internal handling of abuse reports.

title: Jury selection begins in Danny Masterson rape retrial
summary: Danny Masterson's retrial on three rape counts began in Los Angeles, with the judge again permitting limited testimony about the Church of Scientology.

title: Arizona appeals court upholds clergy privilege in child abuse case
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: An appeals court ruled church clergy could invoke clergy-penitent privilege in litigation over the Bisbee abuse case.

title: Gov. Wes Moore signs Child Victims Act, ending time limit on abuse lawsuits
summary: Moore signed the law removing the statute of limitations for civil child sexual abuse claims. It set per-claim damage caps of $890,000 against public entities and $1.5 million against private ones.

title: Maryland attorney general report details abuse of more than 600 children in Archdiocese of Baltimore
summary: A redacted report from the Maryland attorney general accused more than 150 clergy and others affiliated with the Archdiocese of Baltimore of abusing over 600 children across eight decades and documented a long-running cover-up by church officials.

title: Federal district judge upholds Boy Scouts' $2.46 billion bankruptcy settlement
summary: U.S. District Judge Richard Andrews affirmed the bankruptcy court's confirmation of the Boy Scouts plan, finding it a good-faith effort to resolve more than 80,000 abuse claims. Some survivors and insurers continued to appeal.

title: Pope makes revised Vos estis abuse law permanent
summary: An updated version of the 2019 law took permanent effect and extended accountability to lay leaders of church associations.

title: Former FCI Dublin warden sentenced to nearly six years
summary: Garcia was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison for sexually abusing incarcerated women.

title: Former SBC president Johnny Hunt sues denomination and Guidepost for defamation
summary: Hunt, who was accused in the Guidepost report, filed suit seeking damages and disputing the report's findings.

title: Maryland Senate overwhelmingly passes Child Victims Act
summary: The Senate approved the bill eliminating the civil statute of limitations for child sexual abuse claims, including against public institutions.

title: Albany diocese files for bankruptcy amid flood of abuse lawsuits
summary: The Diocese of Albany filed for Chapter 11 protection, facing more than 400 Child Victims Act lawsuits.

title: Diocese of Santa Rosa files for bankruptcy after nearly 200 abuse lawsuits
summary: The Diocese of Santa Rosa filed for Chapter 11 protection after nearly 200 suits were filed under California's lookback window.

title: B.C. judge certifies class action over Christian Brothers abuse at Vancouver schools
summary: A Vancouver judge allowed a class action to proceed against two Catholic schools over alleged abuse by Christian Brothers, including men previously linked to Mount Cashel.

title: Weinstein sentenced to 16 years in Los Angeles case
summary: A Los Angeles judge sentenced Weinstein to 16 years in prison for his California rape and sexual assault conviction, to be served after his New York sentence.

title: California law opens three-year window for adult survivors' time-barred claims
summary: AB 2777, effective Jan. 1, 2023, revived expired civil claims by adult sexual assault survivors against entities alleged to have covered up abuse, through 2026.

title: R. Kelly sentenced to 20 years in Chicago case, mostly concurrent
summary: Judge Harry Leinenweber sentenced Kelly to 20 years, with 19 to run concurrently with his New York term, effectively adding one year.

title: Portuguese inquiry finds nearly 5,000 children abused by clergy since 1950
summary: An independent commission commissioned by Portugal's bishops validated 512 testimonies and estimated at least 4,815 victims.

title: Activision Blizzard pays $35 million to settle SEC workplace misconduct disclosure case
summary: The SEC said Activision Blizzard lacked controls to assess workplace misconduct complaints for disclosure and violated whistleblower rules; the company paid $35 million without admitting or denying the findings.

title: Judge jails Hadden ahead of sentencing
summary: A federal judge revoked Hadden's bail and ordered him jailed pending sentencing after victims urged detention.

title: Cook County prosecutors drop state sex abuse charges against R. Kelly
summary: State's Attorney Kim Foxx dropped the 2019 state charges, citing Kelly's lengthy federal sentences.

title: Federal jury convicts Hadden of luring patients across state lines for abuse
summary: A federal jury found Hadden guilty of four counts of enticing women to travel to New York for unlawful sexual activity.

title: Time's Up halts operations and shifts resources to legal defense fund
summary: Time's Up said it would cease operations and lay off staff, transferring remaining funds to its legal defense fund after a period of turmoil.

title: Sandusky files new post-conviction appeal in Centre County
summary: Sandusky's lawyers filed another petition challenging his conviction, which prosecutors opposed.

title: Dispute over SBC abuse hotline highlights struggles to implement reforms
summary: A disagreement over handling calls to the Guidepost-run abuse hotline raised questions about the pace of reform.

title: SEC charges Easterbrook with misleading investors about his firing
summary: The SEC charged Easterbrook with misleading investors about the circumstances of his termination; he agreed to a $400,000 penalty and an officer-and-director bar without admitting or denying the findings.

title: U.S. Virgin Islands sues JPMorgan over Epstein
summary: The Virgin Islands accused JPMorgan of knowingly facilitating Epstein's sex trafficking by keeping him as a client for years.

title: Nearly 300 former detainees sue L.A. County over alleged sexual abuse in juvenile facilities
summary: A lawsuit filed Dec. 20 on behalf of 279 former detainees alleges probation and detention staff sexually abused youths at county juvenile halls and camps over several decades. The suit claims the county failed to screen, train and supervise its employees.

title: Los Angeles jury convicts Weinstein of rape and sexual assault
summary: A Los Angeles jury found Weinstein guilty of rape and two other sexual offenses involving one woman, acquitted him on one count and deadlocked on others.

title: Senate report details widespread sexual abuse of women in federal prisons
summary: A Senate subcommittee investigation led by Sen. Jon Ossoff found BOP employees sexually abused women in at least two-thirds of federal women's prisons, including Dublin.

title: Jury convicts former FCI Dublin warden Ray Garcia of sexually abusing inmates
summary: A federal jury convicted Garcia on all counts of sexually abusing three incarcerated women. It was the first trial among several cases against Dublin staff.

title: 38 women sue James Toback and the Harvard Club under Adult Survivors Act
summary: Dozens of women filed suit in New York alleging sexual misconduct by Toback over decades and naming the Harvard Club as a defendant.

title: Five women sue Bill Cosby and NBCUniversal under New York's Adult Survivors Act
summary: Five women, including former Cosby Show actors Lili Bernard and Eden Tirl, sued Cosby and accused NBCUniversal and production companies of negligence; Cosby denied the allegations.

title: Five women sue Cosby and NBCUniversal under New York Adult Survivors Act
summary: Five women, including former Cosby Show actresses Lili Bernard and Eden Tirl, sued Cosby for assault and named NBCUniversal and two production companies as defendants on negligence claims under New York's one-year lookback window. Cosby's spokesman called the suit frivolous.

title: Epstein estate settles U.S. Virgin Islands lawsuit for over $105 million
summary: The estate agreed to pay the territory more than $105 million plus proceeds from the sale of Great St. James island to resolve its civil racketeering suit.

title: Danny Masterson rape trial ends in mistrial after jury deadlocks
summary: A Los Angeles judge declared a mistrial after jurors could not reach unanimous verdicts on any of the three rape counts against Danny Masterson; prosecutors said they would retry him.

title: Survivors sue JPMorgan and Deutsche Bank over Epstein ties
summary: Women who say Epstein abused them filed proposed class actions in New York accusing JPMorgan Chase and Deutsche Bank of enabling his sex trafficking; the banks denied wrongdoing.

title: Former camper sues Kanakuk alleging fraud in 2010 abuse settlement
summary: A former camper abused by Pete Newman sued Kanakuk, its CEO and its insurer, alleging his family was misled into a confidential 2010 settlement by claims that leaders did not know of Newman's conduct. Kanakuk declined to comment on pending litigation.

title: CBS and Moonves to pay $30.5 million to resolve New York attorney general probe
summary: The New York attorney general said CBS executives worked to conceal assault allegations against Les Moonves, including tips from an LAPD captain, while Moonves sold stock; CBS, Paramount and Moonves agreed to pay $30.5 million, most of it to shareholders, and adopt reforms.

title: Pennsylvania AG charges four Jehovah's Witnesses members with abusing children
summary: Attorney General Josh Shapiro announced the first charges from the grand jury probe, involving alleged abuse of 19 children.

title: Weinstein's Los Angeles sex crimes trial opens
summary: Opening statements began in Weinstein's second criminal trial, in Los Angeles, where he faced rape and sexual assault charges involving multiple women.

title: Final IICSA report recommends mandatory reporting and national redress scheme
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The inquiry's final report made 20 recommendations, including a legal duty to report child sexual abuse, a national redress scheme and a child protection authority.

title: Jury convicts Heaps on five counts involving two patients
summary: A jury convicted Heaps on five felony counts, acquitted him on seven and deadlocked on the rest; he was taken into custody.

title: IICSA publishes final report on child sexual abuse in England and Wales
source: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The seven-year inquiry, which included investigations of the Catholic Church and Benedictine schools, issued its final recommendations including mandatory reporting.

title: Jury finds Kevin Spacey not liable in Anthony Rapp lawsuit
summary: A federal civil jury in Manhattan found Anthony Rapp had not proven that Kevin Spacey touched him sexually in 1986, rejecting his $40 million claim.

title: Columbia and NewYork-Presbyterian to pay $165 million to Hadden accusers
summary: A $165 million settlement with 147 women brought payouts related to Hadden to about $236 million.

title: Michigan Supreme Court declines review, ending Klages prosecution
summary: The Michigan Supreme Court denied the attorney general's request to review the reversal of Kathie Klages' conviction, leaving the conviction vacated.

title: New book by LA Times reporter details how USC scandals nearly went untold
summary: Times journalist Paul Pringle published an account of the reporting behind the Tyndall and Puliafito stories and the obstacles the newsroom faced.

title: Judge approves fund to distribute Michigan's $490 million Anderson settlement
summary: A federal judge approved the fund for Anderson survivors, with $30 million reserved for future claimants; regents chair Paul Brown apologized.

title: Sixth Circuit revives Strauss lawsuits against Ohio State
summary: A divided federal appeals panel ruled the survivors' Title IX lawsuits could proceed, reversing the dismissal on statute-of-limitations grounds.

title: R. Kelly convicted on child pornography and enticement charges in Chicago
summary: A Chicago federal jury convicted Kelly on six counts including producing child pornography and enticing minors, while acquitting him of conspiring to obstruct his 2008 trial; two co-defendants were acquitted.

title: Judge confirms $2.46 billion Boy Scouts reorganization plan for more than 80,000 abuse claimants
summary: Bankruptcy Judge Laurie Selber Silverstein approved a $2.46 billion plan funded by the BSA, local councils, settling insurers and sponsoring organizations, which in return are shielded from Scout-related abuse suits. A $250 million deal with the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints was dropped after the judge found its release too broad, and objectors said they would appeal.

title: Judge limits clergy-privilege defense in Arizona church abuse case
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: A Cochise County judge ruled the church could not broadly rely on clergy-penitent privilege in the Bisbee civil case.

title: Justice Department opens investigation into Southern Baptist Convention
summary: SBC leaders disclosed that the DOJ had launched an investigation involving multiple SBC entities related to abuse.

title: AP investigation: church abuse help line steered reports to lawyers, abuse continued for years
institution: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
summary: AP reported that church officials in Bisbee, Arizona, did not report a member's admitted abuse to authorities after calling the church's help line, which routes calls to a law firm.

title: Judge rejects parts of Boy Scouts' $2.7 billion abuse settlement, including church contribution
summary: Bankruptcy Judge Laurie Selber Silverstein approved much of the settlement framework but declined to approve certain provisions, including the $250 million Latter-day Saints contribution as structured, requiring revisions before confirmation.

title: Pope Francis apologizes in Canada for abuses at church-run residential schools
summary: Speaking at Maskwacis, Alberta, Pope Francis apologized for the role of Catholics in Canada's residential school system, where Indigenous children suffered abuse including sexual abuse.

title: Ohio State settles with seven more Strauss survivors
summary: Seven additional settlements brought Ohio State's total to 296 survivors and more than $60 million.

title: Telford inquiry finds more than 1,000 children exploited over decades
summary: Tom Crowther KC's independent inquiry found over 1,000 children in Telford were sexually exploited and that authorities ignored the abuse, partly over concerns about race; police and council apologised.

title: R. Kelly sentenced to 30 years in federal prison
summary: U.S. District Judge Ann Donnelly sentenced Kelly to 30 years in prison for racketeering and sex trafficking.

title: Ghislaine Maxwell sentenced to 20 years in prison
summary: Judge Alison Nathan sentenced Maxwell to 20 years for helping Epstein sexually abuse underage girls.

title: Civil jury finds Cosby sexually abused a teenager at Playboy Mansion in 1975
summary: A Santa Monica jury found Cosby liable for sexually abusing a 16-year-old girl in 1975 and awarded her $500,000 in damages. Cosby, who denied the claim, did not attend the trial.

title: Activision board review says executives did not ignore harassment
summary: An Activision Blizzard board review concluded there was no evidence senior executives ignored or tried to cover up harassment, a finding criticized by employee advocates.

title: Lawsuit alleges sexual abuse at L.A. County's MacLaren Hall children's shelter
summary: A lawsuit filed on behalf of former residents alleges that children placed at the county-run MacLaren Hall emergency shelter were sexually abused over decades. The claims accuse the county of failing to protect children in its care.

title: Southern Baptists overwhelmingly approve abuse reforms in Anaheim
summary: Messengers backed creating a database of credibly accused ministers and an implementation task force.

title: About 90 gymnasts including Biles and Raisman seek $1 billion from FBI
summary: Around 90 survivors, including Simone Biles, Aly Raisman and McKayla Maroney, filed administrative claims totaling more than $1 billion against the FBI over its failure to stop Nassar after 2015 reports.

title: UK prosecutors authorize indecent assault charges against Weinstein
summary: Britain's Crown Prosecution Service authorized two counts of indecent assault against Weinstein over allegations involving a woman in London in 1996.

title: New York appeals court upholds Weinstein's rape conviction
summary: An intermediate New York appellate court rejected Weinstein's appeal and affirmed his 2020 conviction and 23-year sentence, finding the trial judge's rulings were proper.

title: New Hampshire governor signs $100 million settlement fund for youth center abuse victims
summary: Gov. Chris Sununu signed legislation creating a $100 million fund to settle claims by people abused at the Youth Development Center. Some victims' lawyers criticized the fund's caps and terms.

title: SBC releases previously secret list of accused abusers
summary: Executive Committee leaders published an internal list kept by staff of hundreds of ministers and others accused of abuse.

title: Justice Department declines to charge FBI agents over Nassar probe
summary: The Justice Department said it would not prosecute two former FBI agents faulted by the inspector general over the Nassar investigation, saying the evidence was insufficient while not endorsing their conduct.

title: Kevin Spacey charged in UK with sexual assault of three men
summary: The Crown Prosecution Service authorized four sexual assault charges against Kevin Spacey involving three men in incidents from 2005 to 2013; further charges were added later. Spacey denied the allegations.

title: Lisa Bloom's firm to pay Steve Wynn to resolve his defamation suit
summary: Attorney Lisa Bloom's firm agreed to pay to settle a defamation lawsuit Steve Wynn filed over statements made while she represented women accusing him of misconduct.

title: UCLA agrees to $374.4 million more, bringing Heaps payouts near $700 million
summary: A $374.4 million settlement with 312 plaintiffs brought total Heaps-related payments to nearly $700 million, a record for a public university.

title: Guidepost report finds SBC leaders stonewalled survivors and protected the institution for decades
summary: The independent report found Executive Committee leaders mishandled abuse reports and resisted reforms, and included an allegation against former SBC president Johnny Hunt.

title: Preliminary hearing continues in Tyndall criminal case
summary: Former patients testified as the lengthy preliminary hearing on the felony charges against Tyndall continued.

title: USC settles suits with 80 former students over campus doctor Dennis Kelly
summary: USC settled lawsuits brought by 80 former students, mostly gay and bisexual men, who alleged sexual misconduct by former men's health physician Dennis Kelly; terms were not disclosed.

title: Hundreds of children allegedly abused at New Hampshire's state youth center, Globe examines
summary: The Globe examined allegations by hundreds of former residents that they were abused at the state-run youth detention center over decades. The state faced a growing wave of civil suits.

title: Nassar survivors file claims against the FBI
summary: Dozens of survivors filed administrative claims against the FBI over its mishandling of 2015 reports about Nassar, the first step toward suing the federal government.

title: Paramount and Moonves agree to $14.75 million settlement with CBS shareholders
summary: Paramount Global and Les Moonves agreed to pay $14.75 million to settle a securities class action alleging CBS misled investors about its handling of misconduct allegations against Moonves.

title: Ohio State reaches two more settlements covering 57 Strauss survivors
summary: Two settlements totaling about $2 million covered 57 survivors whose suits had been dismissed, bringing the total to 289 survivors and $59.8 million.

title: Texas prosecutors drop evidence-tampering charge against ex-USA Gymnastics CEO Steve Penny
summary: Walker County, Texas prosecutors dismissed the tampering charge against Steve Penny over documents removed from the Karolyi Ranch, citing insufficient evidence. Penny had pleaded not guilty.

title: Leaked Hillsong NYC report finds misconduct beyond Carl Lentz
summary: An investigation commissioned by Hillsong described sexual misconduct and abuse of power at its New York church.

title: Judge approves Activision Blizzard's $18 million EEOC settlement
summary: A federal judge approved the consent decree resolving the EEOC's harassment and discrimination case against Activision Blizzard.

title: Brian Houston resigns from Hillsong after board findings on conduct with women
summary: Houston resigned after the church disclosed two complaints about his conduct with women.

title: U.S. Supreme Court declines to review ruling that freed Cosby
summary: The Supreme Court turned down Montgomery County prosecutors' request to reinstate Cosby's conviction, ending the criminal case.

title: Ending forced arbitration for harassment claims signed into law, backed by Gretchen Carlson
summary: President Biden signed a law barring mandatory arbitration of sexual assault and harassment claims; Carlson, whose Fox contract had an arbitration clause, championed the bill.

title: Prince Andrew settles Virginia Giuffre's lawsuit
summary: Prince Andrew reached an out-of-court settlement with Giuffre, without admitting liability, including a donation to her charity.

title: UC settles Heaps lawsuits by 200-plus women for $243.6 million
summary: The University of California agreed to pay $243.6 million to settle suits by more than 200 women who accused Heaps.

title: AP investigation finds culture of sexual abuse at FCI Dublin women's prison
summary: An AP investigation described a permissive and toxic culture at FCI Dublin that enabled staff sexual abuse of incarcerated women for years.

title: Brian Houston steps aside as Hillsong global senior pastor ahead of trial
summary: Houston stepped back from leadership while he prepared to contest the concealment charge.

title: Benedict XVI acknowledges faulty testimony to Munich abuse inquiry
summary: The retired pope corrected his statement and acknowledged attending a 1980 meeting about an abusive priest, attributing the error to an editing mistake.

title: Munich report finds Benedict XVI failed to act on abuse cases
summary: A law firm report commissioned by the Munich archdiocese said then-Archbishop Joseph Ratzinger mishandled four abuse cases in the 1970s and 1980s.

title: Appeals court revives Masterson accusers' harassment suit against Scientology
summary: A California appeals court reversed an order sending the women's harassment claims to Scientology religious arbitration, allowing their lawsuit against the church and Masterson to proceed in court.

title: University of Michigan agrees to $490 million settlement with Anderson survivors
summary: Michigan agreed to pay $490 million to more than 1,000 people who said they were abused by Anderson, one of the largest such settlements by a university.

title: Prince Andrew stripped of military titles and royal patronages
summary: Buckingham Palace said Prince Andrew's military affiliations and royal patronages were returned to the Queen and he would stop using HRH, after a U.S. judge let Giuffre's suit proceed.

title: Preliminary vote tally shows Boy Scouts plan short of targeted survivor support
summary: A preliminary voting report showed about 73% of abuse claimants backed the reorganization plan, below the 75% the Boy Scouts sought given the plan's third-party releases.

title: Ghislaine Maxwell convicted of sex trafficking for Epstein
summary: A federal jury found Maxwell guilty on five of six counts, including sex trafficking of a minor.

title: Biden signs defense bill moving sexual assault prosecutions to independent lawyers
summary: Biden signed the fiscal 2022 defense authorization, which created independent special trial counsel to handle sexual assault cases.

title: Michigan appeals court overturns Klages conviction
summary: The Michigan Court of Appeals reversed Kathie Klages' conviction, finding insufficient evidence that her false statements were material to the Nassar investigation.

title: Appeals court upholds dismissal of charges against Simon
summary: The Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of charges against Simon and criticized the prosecution's investigation.

title: Ousted McDonald's CEO Easterbrook returns $105 million
summary: Easterbrook agreed to return more than $105 million to settle McDonald's lawsuit accusing him of concealing other relationships with employees.

title: Congress sends defense bill overhauling military sexual assault prosecutions to Biden
summary: The Senate passed the annual defense bill moving sexual assault prosecutions to independent military prosecutors and incorporating elements of the Guillen act.

title: Chubb's Century Indemnity agrees to contribute $800 million to Boy Scouts survivor fund
summary: Century Indemnity and affiliated Chubb companies, the Boy Scouts' primary insurer, agreed to pay $800 million into the abuse survivors' trust, pushing the proposed total toward $2.7 billion.

title: Nassar survivors reach $380 million settlement with USA Gymnastics and USOPC
summary: A bankruptcy judge approved a $380 million settlement among USA Gymnastics, the USOPC, their insurers and hundreds of survivors, ending the bankruptcy case.

title: Columbia and NewYork-Presbyterian agree to $71.5 million fund for Hadden accusers
summary: Columbia and NewYork-Presbyterian agreed to a $71.5 million settlement with 79 women who accused Hadden.

title: Ghislaine Maxwell sex trafficking trial opens in Manhattan
summary: Prosecutors told jurors Maxwell and Epstein were partners in the abuse of teenage girls as her federal trial began; her lawyers argued she was being blamed for Epstein's crimes.

title: Kevin Spacey ordered to pay $31 million to 'House of Cards' producer over firing losses
summary: Court filings showed an arbitrator ordered Kevin Spacey to pay about $31 million to MRC, finding he breached his contract's harassment policies and caused losses when the studio rewrote House of Cards.

title: WSJ reports CEO Bobby Kotick knew of misconduct claims; staff walk out again
summary: A Wall Street Journal report said Kotick knew of sexual misconduct allegations for years without fully informing the board, prompting calls for his resignation. Kotick called the report inaccurate.

title: Barclays CEO Jes Staley steps down after regulator's Epstein probe
summary: Staley, a former JPMorgan executive who oversaw Epstein's accounts, left Barclays after UK regulators reached preliminary conclusions about how he described his relationship with Epstein.

title: USC admits troubling delay in warning campus about fraternity drugging and assault reports
summary: President Carol Folt acknowledged USC was slow to alert students to reports of drugging and sexual assault allegedly connected to a campus fraternity.

title: Former NFL player Jon Vaughn camps outside Michigan president's home
summary: Former Michigan running back Jon Vaughn staged a sit-in outside President Mark Schlissel's residence demanding accountability for Anderson's abuse.

title: Former Cosby Show actress Lili Bernard sues Cosby in New Jersey
summary: Actress Lili Bernard, who appeared on The Cosby Show, filed a civil suit alleging Cosby drugged and sexually assaulted her in 1990, using a New Jersey law that extended filing deadlines. Cosby denied the allegations.

title: SBC Executive Committee chief Ronnie Floyd resigns amid abuse probe dispute
summary: Floyd stepped down as president of the Executive Committee following the vote to waive privilege in the abuse investigation.

title: California's Silenced No More Act widens limits on workplace NDAs
summary: California enacted SB 331, extending the ban on nondisclosure provisions in settlements beyond sexual harassment to all forms of workplace harassment and discrimination.

title: Complaints of alleged abuse by Anderson surpass 2,100
summary: The Detroit News reported that complaints of alleged abuse by Anderson had exceeded 2,100.

title: Pope Francis expresses shame over French church abuse findings
summary: Francis voiced shame at the church's long failure to put victims first after the Sauvé report.

title: Tyndall accusers call for investigation of top USC officials
summary: Former patients and their advocates urged authorities to investigate whether USC administrators knew of Tyndall's alleged abuse and failed to act.

title: SBC Executive Committee waives attorney-client privilege for abuse investigation
summary: After weeks of dispute, the Executive Committee voted to waive privilege so Guidepost Solutions could access legal records.

title: Sauvé report estimates 330,000 children abused in French church since 1950
summary: The CIASE found roughly 216,000 minors were abused by clergy, rising to about 330,000 including lay church workers, and described a systemic failure.

title: FCI Dublin warden Ray Garcia charged with sexually abusing an inmate
summary: Federal prosecutors charged the warden of the women's prison in Dublin, California, with sexual abuse of a woman in his custody. He was presumed innocent.

title: Activision Blizzard reaches $18 million deal with EEOC
summary: The EEOC sued Activision Blizzard over sexual harassment and discrimination and the company simultaneously agreed to an $18 million fund to compensate eligible workers.

title: R. Kelly convicted of racketeering and sex trafficking in New York
summary: A Brooklyn federal jury found Kelly guilty on all nine counts, including racketeering and Mann Act violations, after a six-week trial in which several accusers testified.

title: Federal judge dismisses Strauss lawsuits on statute-of-limitations grounds
summary: A federal judge dismissed several lawsuits against Ohio State, ruling the Title IX claims were filed too late; plaintiffs appealed.

title: Biles, Maroney, Raisman and Nichols testify to Senate about FBI failures
summary: Four elite gymnasts told the Senate Judiciary Committee the FBI ignored and mishandled their reports, following a Justice Department inspector general report criticizing agents; FBI Director Christopher Wray apologized.

title: Hartford raises Boy Scouts deal to $787 million; Latter-day Saints church agrees to pay $250 million
summary: The Hartford agreed to a tentative $787 million contribution to the survivors' fund, and the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, formerly the largest troop sponsor, agreed to pay $250 million in exchange for releases from abuse claims.

title: Judge lets sex-trafficking and assault claims against Ed Henry proceed
source: New York Daily News (via Wigdor LLP)
summary: A federal judge in Manhattan declined to dismiss key claims in the lawsuit against Henry, including sex-trafficking allegations, and allowed some claims against Fox to continue.

title: Inquiry says religious groups failing children over sexual abuse
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: A report on religious organisations found many faith groups lacked basic child protection and discouraged reporting.

title: Time's Up CEO resigns amid fallout over Cuomo scandal
summary: Tina Tchen stepped down as Time's Up chief executive after reports that group leaders had advised New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo's team as he faced harassment allegations.

title: Bankruptcy judge gives conditional approval to Boy Scouts' $850 million survivor deal
summary: A Delaware bankruptcy judge allowed the Boy Scouts to enter the $850 million settlement but rejected provisions on paying claimant lawyers' fees and on backing out of the Hartford agreement.

title: Jury selection begins in R. Kelly's Brooklyn sex trafficking trial
summary: Jury selection opened in Kelly's long-delayed federal racketeering and sex trafficking trial in Brooklyn.

title: Virginia Giuffre sues Prince Andrew in New York
summary: Giuffre, who has spoken publicly about Epstein's abuse, filed a civil suit alleging Prince Andrew sexually abused her when she was 17; he denied the allegations.

title: Australian police charge Hillsong founder Brian Houston with concealing father's abuse
summary: New South Wales police charged Houston with concealing a serious indictable offense involving abuse by his late father, Frank Houston.

title: Spanier released from jail after serving 58 days
summary: Spanier was released from the Centre County Correctional Facility after serving nearly all of his two-month sentence.

title: Blizzard president J. Allen Brack steps down amid harassment scandal
summary: Blizzard Entertainment president J. Allen Brack left the company in the wake of the California lawsuit and employee protests.

title: Grand jury indicts 10 of 11 former YDC employees in abuse probe
summary: A grand jury indicted 10 of the 11 former Youth Development Center employees arrested earlier in the year on multiple counts tied to alleged sexual abuse of residents. The defendants are presumed innocent.

title: Fox Business producer sues alleging unwanted advances by Andrew Napolitano
summary: An associate producer sued Fox News alleging unwanted advances by legal analyst Andrew Napolitano and a dismissive response from management. Fox said it took action on the Napolitano complaint and called other claims baseless.

title: Ex-cardinal McCarrick criminally charged in Massachusetts with assaulting a teenager in 1974
summary: McCarrick was charged in Dedham District Court with indecent assault and battery on a person over 14, stemming from an alleged 1974 assault at a wedding reception at Wellesley College. He became the first U.S. cardinal criminally charged with sexual abuse of a minor.

title: Activision Blizzard employees walk out over company's response to lawsuit
summary: Employees staged a walkout protesting leadership's initial response to the state lawsuit and demanding changes to policies on harassment and arbitration.

title: Inquiry finds Lambeth council exposed children in care to decades of abuse
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The Lambeth report found a culture of cover-up meant hundreds of children in the council's care were subjected to sexual and physical abuse.

title: Catholic Church sells assets to pay Mount Cashel survivors
summary: The Archdiocese of St. John's began selling churches and property to compensate Mount Cashel survivors, though their lawyer warned proceeds would fall short.

title: California sues Activision Blizzard alleging harassment and 'frat boy' culture
summary: California's Department of Fair Employment and Housing sued Activision Blizzard alleging widespread sexual harassment and discrimination against women. The company disputed the claims.

title: Weinstein extradited from New York to Los Angeles to face sex crime charges
summary: Weinstein was transferred from a New York prison to Los Angeles County custody to face charges of rape and sexual assault involving several women in California.

title: DOJ inspector general finds FBI badly mishandled Nassar allegations
summary: The Justice Department inspector general found the FBI's Indianapolis office made fundamental errors after learning of Nassar allegations in 2015, failing to act promptly or notify authorities, and that officials later gave inaccurate accounts.

title: Judge gives final approval to $73 million Heaps class settlement
summary: A federal judge granted final approval of the $73 million class-action settlement for former Heaps patients.

title: Commission issues 80 recommendations; Austin orders military sexual assault reforms
summary: The Independent Review Commission found the military unequipped to address sexual assault, and Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin ordered changes including shifting prosecution authority.

title: Boy Scouts reach $850 million settlement with tens of thousands of abuse survivors
summary: The Boy Scouts and its local councils agreed to contribute $850 million to a trust for abuse survivors under a deal with major claimant groups. It was the largest such settlement involving a youth organization at the time.

title: Pennsylvania Supreme Court overturns Cosby conviction; he is freed from prison
summary: The state Supreme Court vacated Cosby's conviction, ruling that a former district attorney's earlier promise not to prosecute should have barred the charges, and released him after nearly three years in prison. The ruling did not find him innocent.

title: New York City fines Fox News $1 million over harassment and retaliation
summary: The NYC Commission on Human Rights fined Fox News $1 million, its largest such penalty, and required policy changes after finding harassment and retaliation violations.

title: Report says federal grand jury examining USA Swimming over abuse cover-up and insurance
summary: Salon reported that a federal grand jury in Manhattan was investigating USA Swimming over alleged concealment of abuse cases and insurance practices; prosecutors declined to comment. The organization faced dozens of civil abuse claims.

title: Southern Baptist messengers approve task force and independent review of Executive Committee
summary: Messengers in Nashville overwhelmingly voted for a third-party investigation of how the Executive Committee handled abuse claims.

title: Former players allege Bo Schembechler knew of Anderson abuse
summary: At a news conference, accusers including a Schembechler family member alleged the late coach was told of the abuse and did not act; other family members denied he knew.

title: Leaked letters prompt Southern Baptist pastors to demand inquiry into abuse handling
summary: After letters from former ethics chief Russell Moore alleging mistreatment of abuse survivors became public, pastors called for an independent investigation of the Executive Committee.

title: Parole board denies Cosby release after he refuses sex offender treatment
summary: The Pennsylvania parole board denied Cosby parole, citing his refusal to take part in a required sex offender treatment program.

title: Spanier ordered to serve two months in jail
summary: After his appeals ran out, Spanier was ordered to serve two months in county jail followed by house arrest.

title: Grand jury indicts Heaps on 21 counts
source: NBC Palm Springs / City News Service
summary: A Los Angeles County grand jury indicted Heaps on 21 sex-related felony counts involving seven patients.

title: Guards in Epstein death case reach deal sparing them jail
summary: Federal prosecutors agreed to a deferred prosecution deal with the two guards, who admitted falsifying records but avoided prison time.

title: WilmerHale report finds Michigan missed many chances to stop Anderson
summary: The university-commissioned WilmerHale report found staff were told about Anderson's conduct on at least 20 occasions, including complaints allegedly relayed to Bo Schembechler and Don Canham.

title: Ohio State launches individual settlement program for remaining Strauss cases
summary: Ohio State opened a 120-day individual settlement program for survivors in five active cases, targeting average awards comparable to earlier settlements.

title: Tyndall settlement leaves some survivors bitter over payout disparities
summary: The Times reported wide disparities between payments to plaintiffs in the state-court deal and those in the federal class settlement.

title: Pentagon panel recommends ending commanders' control of sexual assault prosecutions
summary: An independent review commission recommended moving decisions on prosecuting sexual assault cases from commanders to independent military lawyers.

title: The Hartford agrees to pay $650 million to settle Boy Scouts abuse coverage claims
summary: Insurer The Hartford reached a $650 million agreement with the Boy Scouts to resolve its coverage obligations for abuse claims. Survivor groups objected that the amount was far too low.

title: France's top court confirms Cardinal Barbarin's acquittal
summary: The Court of Cassation upheld an appeals ruling that cleared Barbarin of failing to report abuse.

title: Former New Hampshire youth center workers charged in sex abuse investigation
summary: State authorities announced arrests of former staff at the Youth Development Center in Manchester, accused of sexually assaulting youths in their care decades ago. The arrests came from the attorney general's YDC task force created in 2019.

title: Michigan attorney general closes MSU probe after university keeps Nassar documents privileged
summary: Attorney General Dana Nessel ended her office's investigation of Michigan State's handling of Nassar after the university declined to waive attorney-client privilege over thousands of documents.

title: Report reexamines Kanakuk Kamps abuse and nondisclosure agreements with victims
summary: Reporting revisited abuse by former Kanakuk director Pete Newman, imprisoned since 2010, and found the camp had kept promoting him despite earlier complaints. Many families settled under NDAs, prompting calls for the camp to release victims from them.

title: Harvard sanctions professor Martin Nowak over Epstein involvement
summary: Harvard sanctioned mathematician Martin Nowak and closed his research program after finding he gave Epstein extensive campus access in violation of university policy.

title: USC agrees to $852 million settlement, bringing Tyndall payouts above $1.1 billion
summary: USC reached an $852 million settlement with about 710 women in state court, which with the federal class deal brought total payouts to more than $1.1 billion, the largest sexual abuse settlement in higher education history.

title: Former Olympic coach John Geddert charged, then dies by suicide
summary: Michigan's attorney general charged Geddert with human trafficking, sexual assault and other crimes; he was found dead hours later.

title: Judge declines to halt Weinstein Company plan pending objectors' appeal
summary: The bankruptcy judge refused a request from objecting accusers to pause the confirmed plan while they appealed.

title: Law firm report finds Ravi Zacharias engaged in sexual misconduct
summary: An investigation commissioned by RZIM found extensive misconduct by Zacharias, who died in 2020, and the ministry apologized.

title: Pilots allege abuse by Anderson during FAA physicals
summary: Pilots came forward alleging abuse by Anderson, who performed more than 4,000 FAA medical exams.

title: Bankruptcy judge approves Weinstein Company plan with about $17 million for accusers
summary: A Delaware bankruptcy judge confirmed a liquidation plan setting aside roughly $17 million for people with sexual misconduct claims against Weinstein.

title: Leon Black to step down as Apollo CEO after review finds $158 million in Epstein payments
summary: An outside review found Black paid Epstein about $158 million for tax and estate advice; it found no involvement in Epstein's crimes, and Black said he would step down as CEO.

title: Supreme Court of Canada declines archdiocese's Mount Cashel appeal
summary: The Supreme Court refused to hear the archdiocese's appeal, leaving it liable for abuse at Mount Cashel and ending a two-decade legal fight.

title: Irish state and church apologize over mother and baby homes
summary: Taoiseach Micheál Martin delivered a state apology and Catholic leaders also apologized after the commission's findings.

title: Mother and baby homes report finds 9,000 children died
institution: Mother and Baby Homes Commission of Investigation
summary: The commission's final report found about 9,000 children died in the 18 institutions examined, many of them run by Catholic orders, and described a deeply misogynistic culture.

title: Appeals court rejects Nassar's bid for a new sentencing hearing
summary: The Michigan Court of Appeals ruled that Judge Aquilina's comments did not show bias and denied Nassar's request for resentencing.

title: Empowering Athletes Act strengthens oversight of U.S. Olympic system
summary: A federal law enacted in late 2020 gave Congress power to dissolve the USOPC board and decertify governing bodies, and increased funding for the U.S. Center for SafeSport.

title: Paris court convicts former Vatican envoy of sexual assault
summary: Former papal nuncio to France Luigi Ventura received a suspended sentence for sexually assaulting men in Paris.

title: Home Office publishes long-delayed review of grooming gang characteristics
summary: The Home Office released its review of group-based child sexual exploitation after pressure to publish, concluding offenders came from diverse backgrounds and data were poor.

title: Army fires or suspends 14 Fort Hood leaders after independent review
summary: An independent review blamed leadership failures for a climate that tolerated sexual assault and harassment at Fort Hood, leading the Army to remove or suspend 14 officers and soldiers.

title: Federal appeals court reinstates Spanier's child endangerment conviction
summary: The 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled the lower court had improperly vacated Spanier's misdemeanor conviction.

title: Ampleforth College barred from admitting new pupils over safeguarding
summary: The Department for Education ordered the Catholic boarding school to stop taking new pupils after inspectors found safeguarding failings.

title: At least 82,000 sex abuse claims filed against Boy Scouts by bankruptcy deadline
summary: The claims deadline in the Boy Scouts' Chapter 11 case closed with more than 82,000 abuse claims filed, far beyond earlier projections. The volume made the case the largest of its kind in U.S. history.

title: University of California agrees to $73 million class settlement over Heaps
summary: The UC system proposed a $73 million class-action settlement covering thousands of Heaps's former patients plus reforms such as a chaperone policy.

title: DOJ review finds Acosta used poor judgment in Epstein deal
summary: The Office of Professional Responsibility concluded Acosta exercised poor judgment in resolving the federal Epstein investigation but did not commit professional misconduct.

title: Vatican report finds church leaders, including John Paul II, discounted warnings about McCarrick
summary: The Vatican released a 449-page internal report concluding that bishops, cardinals and popes received reports of McCarrick's misconduct for decades, and that Pope John Paul II promoted him despite those warnings.

title: IICSA finds Catholic Church in England and Wales swept abuse under the carpet
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The inquiry's report on the Catholic Church said it put its reputation ahead of victims and criticized Cardinal Vincent Nichols's leadership.

title: Detroit News investigation details decades of missed warnings about Anderson
summary: An in-depth Detroit News report described how the university failed for decades to heed warnings about Anderson.

title: Apollo board orders review of Leon Black's ties to Epstein
summary: Apollo's board hired an outside law firm to review CEO Leon Black's payments to Epstein after reports of tens of millions in transfers.

title: Ohio State reaches $5.8 million settlement with 23 more Strauss survivors
summary: A second settlement of $5.8 million with 23 survivors brought the total to $46.7 million for 185 survivors.

title: Anita Hill-led Hollywood Commission survey finds harassment persists
summary: A survey by the Hollywood Commission found that many entertainment workers still experience harassment and that most doubt perpetrators will be held accountable.

title: Inquiry finds Church of England was 'a hiding place for abusers'
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The Anglican Church report concluded the Church of England put its reputation ahead of victims and failed to respond properly to abuse.

title: Rockville Centre becomes fourth New York diocese to file for bankruptcy
summary: The Long Island diocese, facing more than 200 Child Victims Act lawsuits, filed for Chapter 11 protection.

title: Spa workers accuse Ravi Zacharias of misconduct; RZIM opens investigation
summary: Former employees of spas co-owned by the late apologist alleged sexual harassment, prompting RZIM to hire a law firm.

title: Alphabet settles shareholder suits over harassment, commits $310 million to diversity
summary: Alphabet settled shareholder suits over its handling of misconduct by executives, agreeing to governance reforms and a $310 million diversity and inclusion commitment.

title: I Am Vanessa Guillen Act introduced in Congress
summary: Lawmakers introduced legislation named for the slain Fort Hood soldier to move sexual harassment and assault cases outside the chain of command.

title: Federal prosecutors indict Hadden on enticement charges
summary: Hadden was arrested on a federal indictment accusing him of abusing dozens of patients from 1993 to 2012 and luring victims across state lines.

title: Queensland law requires priests to report abuse disclosed in confession
summary: Following a royal commission recommendation, Queensland passed a law making clergy who fail to report child abuse learned in confession liable to jail.

title: Monks to leave Downside Abbey after abuse scandal
institution: Catholic Church in England and Wales
summary: The Benedictine community decided to leave Downside Abbey and separate from the school following the abuse findings.

title: Klages sentenced to 90 days in jail in Nassar-related case
summary: A judge sentenced Kathie Klages to 90 days in jail and probation for lying to investigators about her knowledge of complaints against Nassar.

title: Heaps now faces 20 felony counts involving seven patients
summary: Prosecutors expanded the case against Heaps to 20 felony counts involving seven patients from 2011 to 2018; he pleaded not guilty.

title: N.L. Court of Appeal rules Archdiocese of St. John's liable for Mount Cashel abuse
summary: The province's appeal court unanimously reversed a 2018 ruling and found the Roman Catholic archdiocese vicariously liable for abuse of boys at Mount Cashel in the 1950s and 1960s.

title: Tyndall pleads not guilty to new felony charges
summary: Tyndall entered not-guilty pleas to the additional charges involving alleged crimes between 2011 and 2015.

title: Lawsuit accuses Ed Henry of rape and names other Fox hosts in harassment claims
summary: A former Fox Business associate producer sued alleging Henry sexually assaulted her, and a former guest commentator joined with harassment claims against several hosts. Henry and Fox denied the allegations.

title: Report: Ousted USC president Nikias received $7.6 million payout
summary: Tax filings showed Nikias received about $7.6 million in compensation after he was pushed out over the Tyndall scandal.

title: Ghislaine Maxwell denied bail, pleads not guilty
summary: A federal judge denied Maxwell bail, calling her a flight risk, after she pleaded not guilty to the charges.

title: Federal judge rejects proposed $18.9 million Weinstein settlement
summary: U.S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein refused to approve a class settlement negotiated with the New York attorney general's office, criticizing how it treated different claimants.

title: Six more felony counts filed against Tyndall
summary: Prosecutors added six counts of sexual assault and battery involving five additional women, bringing the total to 35 felony counts.

title: New York regulator fines Deutsche Bank $150 million over Epstein relationship
source: New York State Department of Financial Services
summary: New York's financial regulator imposed a $150 million penalty on Deutsche Bank, citing compliance failures including its handling of Epstein's accounts.

title: Ghislaine Maxwell arrested on federal charges tied to Epstein
summary: FBI agents arrested Maxwell in New Hampshire on charges that she helped recruit and groom minors for Epstein in the 1990s.

title: Fox News fires anchor Ed Henry after sexual misconduct complaint
summary: Fox fired America's Newsroom co-anchor Ed Henry after an investigation into a former employee's complaint of willful sexual misconduct years earlier.

title: New York AG announces proposed $18.9 million settlement for Weinstein accusers
summary: New York Attorney General Letitia James announced a proposed settlement of about $18.9 million with Weinstein, his former studio and its board to compensate women who alleged misconduct, a deal some accusers criticized.

title: Australia's PM condemns Jehovah's Witnesses and others refusing to join redress scheme
summary: The government threatened funding and charity-status consequences for institutions, including the Jehovah's Witnesses, that declined to join the national redress scheme.

title: Pope moves against Polish bishop accused of shielding abusers
summary: The Vatican sidelined Bishop Edward Janiak of Kalisz under the Vos estis procedures over alleged failures to act on abuse.

title: Judge orders Michigan to halt mass alumni outreach in Anderson case
summary: A federal judge ordered the university to stop contacting more than 300,000 alumni, finding it improperly communicated with potential class members.

title: Diocese of Syracuse files for bankruptcy
summary: The Diocese of Syracuse filed for Chapter 11 protection, moving Child Victims Act suits into bankruptcy court.

title: Danny Masterson charged with raping three women
summary: The Los Angeles County district attorney charged Danny Masterson with three counts of rape involving incidents between 2001 and 2003. Masterson pleaded not guilty.

title: Judge dismisses charges against former MSU President Simon
summary: An Eaton County judge dismissed the charges against Simon, finding insufficient evidence that she lied to investigators.

title: Ohio State to pay $40.9 million to 162 men abused by Strauss
summary: Ohio State finalized a $40.9 million settlement with 162 survivors across 12 lawsuits.

title: Unredacted royal commission findings say Pell knew of abuse
institution: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Previously redacted sections found Pell was aware of child abuse by clergy in Ballarat in the 1970s and failed to act; Pell disputed the findings.

title: Archdiocese of New Orleans files for bankruptcy
summary: The Archdiocese of New Orleans filed for Chapter 11 protection, citing the cost of clergy abuse litigation.

title: Harvard report details Epstein gifts and campus access
summary: A Harvard review found Epstein gave the university millions before his 2008 conviction and continued visiting campus afterward, and the university announced related sanctions and policy changes.

title: University of Michigan says it hopes to settle Anderson lawsuits
summary: Michigan's president and regents chair said the university wanted to resolve claims from hundreds of Anderson accusers.

title: High Court of Australia overturns Pell's convictions
summary: The High Court unanimously quashed Pell's convictions, finding the jury should have had reasonable doubt, and he was released.

title: French priest Bernard Preynat jailed for abusing Scouts
summary: A Lyon court sentenced the defrocked priest to five years in prison for sexually assaulting boy scouts decades earlier.

title: Inquiry criticises internet companies over child abuse online
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The inquiry's internet report found technology companies were failing to do enough to prevent online grooming and the sharing of abuse images.

title: Michigan regents chair Ron Weiser says Anderson abused him
summary: Board of Regents chair Ron Weiser said he was abused by Anderson as a student athlete in the 1960s and declined to recuse himself.

title: Weinstein sentenced to 23 years in prison
summary: Justice James Burke sentenced Weinstein to 23 years in prison for his New York convictions.

title: Ohio State announces settlements in 11 of 18 Strauss lawsuits
summary: Ohio State said it reached monetary settlements covering 11 of 18 pending Strauss lawsuits, with mediation continuing on the rest.

title: Six former wrestlers tell CNN that Jim Jordan knew about Strauss
summary: Six former wrestlers told CNN that Jordan was aware of Strauss's conduct, which Jordan continues to deny.

title: Former football and hockey players sue Michigan over Anderson
summary: Additional lawsuits were filed by former football and hockey players alleging abuse by Anderson.

title: AG Nessel sets conditions for any state probe of Michigan's Anderson response
summary: Attorney General Dana Nessel said a state investigation would require the university to waive privilege and the Legislature to fund it.

title: Former wrestler files first lawsuit against Michigan over Anderson
summary: A former Michigan wrestler filed the first lawsuit alleging the university failed to stop Anderson's abuse.

title: Diocese of Buffalo files for bankruptcy, citing more than 500 abuse claims
summary: The Diocese of Buffalo filed for Chapter 11 protection, acknowledging more than 500 clergy abuse claims.

title: Education Department finds USC failed students in Tyndall case; reforms required
summary: The Office for Civil Rights concluded USC systemically failed to respond to complaints about Tyndall and entered a resolution agreement requiring Title IX reforms and monitoring.

title: Inquiry finds Westminster institutions failed to respond to child abuse claims
institution: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
summary: The Westminster investigation found political parties and institutions showed deference to powerful people and failed to act on allegations, though it found no evidence of an organised network.

title: Jury convicts Weinstein of rape and criminal sexual act, acquits on most serious counts
summary: A Manhattan jury found Weinstein guilty of third-degree rape and a first-degree criminal sexual act but acquitted him of predatory sexual assault.

title: Records show Michigan officials were warned about Anderson decades ago
summary: AP-obtained records show Anderson was pushed out as health service director in 1980 after complaints but continued working with athletes until 2003.

title: Penn State resolves outstanding disputes with the Paterno family
summary: Penn State agreed to cover some Paterno family expenses and settled a 2014 lawsuit by Jay Paterno, with the family agreeing not to push for further review of the scandal.

title: Texas church expelled from SBC for hiring a convicted sex offender as pastor
summary: The SBC Executive Committee voted to disfellowship a Texas congregation over its employment of a registered sex offender as pastor.

title: University of Michigan investigates abuse claims against late doctor Robert Anderson
summary: Michigan announced an outside investigation into allegations that late physician Robert Anderson abused patients during exams for decades, and opened a hotline; prosecutors said no charges were possible.

title: Boy Scouts of America files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy amid wave of abuse lawsuits
summary: The Boy Scouts filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware, pausing hundreds of lawsuits brought after states including New York, New Jersey, Arizona and California opened lookback windows for old abuse claims. The organization planned a survivor compensation trust; its internal files listed 7,819 suspected abusers.

title: Former MSU gymnastics coach Kathie Klages convicted of lying to police
summary: A jury convicted former Michigan State gymnastics coach Kathie Klages of lying to police about when she learned of complaints against Nassar.

title: Former wrestler testifies Jordan pressed him to deny abuse claims
summary: A former Ohio State wrestler testified at a state legislative hearing that Jordan had called pleading with him to dispute his brother's allegations; Jordan denies wrongdoing.

title: Pennsylvania grand jury investigating Jehovah's Witnesses abuse handling
summary: The Inquirer reported a statewide grand jury was examining how the church handled child abuse allegations.

title: NYT investigation describes culture of misogyny inside Victoria's Secret
summary: A New York Times investigation reported allegations of harassment and bullying of models and employees, centered on former marketing chief Ed Razek, who denied them.

title: USA Gymnastics settlement proposal includes Twistars and Geddert contributions
summary: A proposed USA Gymnastics bankruptcy settlement with Nassar survivors included added payments from Twistars and the Gedderts; survivors did not accept the initial plan.

title: SAG-AFTRA issues industry standards for intimacy coordinators
summary: The actors' union released standards and protocols for intimacy coordinators to oversee nude and simulated sex scenes, part of its response to on-set harassment.

title: Judge rejects Sandusky's request for shorter sentence
summary: The judge denied Sandusky's motion to reconsider the reimposed 30-to-60-year sentence.

title: Actress Annabella Sciorra testifies against Weinstein at New York trial
summary: Sciorra testified that Weinstein raped her in the early 1990s; her account was offered to support the predatory sexual assault charges.

title: Police search home and gym of coach John Geddert
summary: Investigators searched the home and former gym of Geddert, the 2012 Olympic women's coach who worked closely with Nassar.

title: Evelyn Yang says she was assaulted by gynecologist Robert Hadden
summary: Evelyn Yang, wife of presidential candidate Andrew Yang, said publicly that Hadden assaulted her while she was pregnant, renewing scrutiny of the case.

title: Cosby asks Pennsylvania Supreme Court to review his conviction
summary: Cosby's lawyers petitioned the state's highest court to overturn his conviction after losing in the Superior Court; the court later agreed to hear the appeal.

title: Montana Supreme Court reverses $35 million verdict against Jehovah's Witnesses
summary: The court held the church was exempt from Montana's mandatory reporting law under a clergy exception.

title: Federal judge says he will approve USC's $215 million Tyndall class settlement
summary: U.S. District Judge Stephen Wilson said he was inclined to grant final approval to the federal class settlement and to appoint a special master to oversee individual awards.

title: Weinstein's New York rape trial begins as Los Angeles prosecutors file new charges
summary: Jury selection began in Manhattan the same day the Los Angeles County district attorney announced rape and sexual battery charges against Weinstein involving two women.

title: California's three-year abuse lawsuit window opens
summary: California's AB 218 lookback window took effect Jan. 1, 2020, allowing thousands of new claims against Catholic dioceses.

title: Attorney general's investigation of MSU's Nassar handling suspended
summary: Michigan's attorney general halted the state's inquiry into Michigan State after the university refused to release privileged documents.

title: Uber to pay $4.4 million to resolve EEOC sexual harassment charge
summary: Uber agreed to a $4.4 million fund for employees after an EEOC investigation found a culture that permitted sexual harassment and retaliation.

title: Pope abolishes pontifical secret in abuse cases
summary: Francis lifted pontifical secrecy over abuse cases, allowing church documents to be shared with civil authorities.

title: Weinstein and former studio reach tentative $25 million deal with accusers
summary: A tentative global settlement funded by insurers would resolve many civil claims against Weinstein and The Weinstein Company's former board without Weinstein admitting wrongdoing.

title: Fox Nation host Britt McHenry sues Fox alleging harassment by co-host
summary: Fox Nation host Britt McHenry sued Fox News alleging sexual harassment by co-host George 'Tyrus' Murdoch and retaliation; Fox and Murdoch disputed the claims.

title: Pennsylvania Superior Court upholds Cosby conviction
summary: A state appeals panel rejected Cosby's challenges, including to the testimony of other accusers and the prosecution's handling of a former DA's non-prosecution promise.

title: New Jersey litigation window opens with new suits including against McCarrick
summary: As New Jersey's two-year lookback window opened, survivors filed new lawsuits against dioceses and former cardinal Theodore McCarrick.

title: Buffalo Bishop Richard Malone resigns over handling of abuse cases
summary: Bishop Richard Malone resigned after revelations that the Diocese of Buffalo kept accused priests off a public list and in ministry.

title: Wynn Resorts settles derivative suit for $41 million, including $20 million from Steve Wynn
summary: Wynn Resorts agreed to settle a shareholder derivative lawsuit over the board's handling of the allegations, with Steve Wynn paying $20 million and insurers $21 million to the company.

title: Sandusky resentenced to the same 30 to 60 years in prison
summary: A visiting judge imposed the same 30-to-60-year prison term at Sandusky's resentencing in Bellefonte.

title: Prince Andrew steps back from royal duties over Epstein ties
summary: Prince Andrew announced he would step back from public duties after a widely criticized BBC interview about his friendship with Epstein.

title: Jail guards on duty when Epstein died charged with falsifying records
summary: Two Metropolitan Correctional Center guards were charged with falsifying records to cover up that they failed to check on Epstein the night he died.

title: Lawsuit says referee warned Jim Jordan about Strauss
summary: A retired wrestling referee alleged in a lawsuit that he told Jordan and head coach Russ Hellickson about Strauss's conduct; Jordan called the claim ridiculous.

title: McDonald's fires CEO Steve Easterbrook over relationship with employee
summary: McDonald's ousted Easterbrook for violating company policy by having a consensual relationship with an employee.

title: Penn State investigates new abuse allegation against Sandusky
summary: Penn State police logged a report alleging Sandusky sexually assaulted a visitor in the Lasch Football Building between 2000 and 2010; the allegation was unproven.

title: 19 women accused Columbia gynecologist Robert Hadden; plea deal spared prison
summary: The Times reported that despite accusations from 19 women, former Columbia OB-GYN Robert Hadden received a 2016 plea deal with no prison time.

title: Los Angeles prosecutors decline Kevin Spacey case after accuser's death
summary: The Los Angeles County district attorney declined to file a sexual battery case against Kevin Spacey because the masseur who accused him had died.

title: California governor signs AB 218, opening a window for old child sexual abuse claims
summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 218, extending California's statute of limitations for childhood sexual abuse and opening a three-year revival window. The law later became the basis for thousands of claims against Los Angeles County.

title: Matt Lauer accused of rape by former NBC colleague in Farrow book
summary: A former NBC News employee whose 2017 complaint led to Matt Lauer's firing alleged in Ronan Farrow's book Catch and Kill that Lauer raped her in 2014. Lauer denied the allegation, saying the encounter was consensual.

title: California law reopens filing window for Tyndall survivors
summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 1510, allowing former patients of Tyndall to revive claims that would otherwise be time-barred; USC had lobbied against the bill.

title: Ohio State's annual safety report lists nearly 1,500 Strauss-related incidents
summary: Ohio State's annual campus safety report attributed nearly 1,500 sexual offense reports to Strauss.

title: Former patients urge UC regents to order independent Heaps investigation
summary: Former patients, including ex-UCLA gymnast Jeanette Antolin, asked the UC Board of Regents for an independent investigation into Heaps.

title: Missouri attorney general refers 12 former clergy for possible prosecution
summary: Attorney General Eric Schmitt's review of Missouri's four dioceses identified 163 accused clergy and referred 12 living former clerics to prosecutors.

title: Diocese of Rochester files for bankruptcy after Child Victims Act suits
summary: The Diocese of Rochester became the first New York diocese to file for Chapter 11 protection after a wave of lawsuits under the Child Victims Act.

title: MIT Media Lab director Joi Ito resigns over Epstein ties
summary: Joi Ito resigned as director of the MIT Media Lab after reporting showed the lab had sought to conceal its financial relationship with Epstein.

title: Education Department fines Michigan State record $4.5 million over Nassar Clery failures
summary: The U.S. Department of Education imposed a $4.5 million fine, the largest ever under the Clery Act, finding Michigan State failed to properly respond to sexual misconduct reports including those involving Nassar.

title: Criminal case against Epstein formally dismissed after his death
